text: Panning is the distribution of a sound signal, whether monaural or a pair of stereo channels, into a new stereo or multi-channel sound field determined by a pan control setting. A typical physical recording console features a pan control for each incoming source channel, which is often an analog knob or slider known as a pan pot (short for "panoramic potentiometer"). This device functions as an analog knob or slider with a position indicator that can range continuously from the 8 o'clock position, representing fully left, to the 4 o'clock position, representing fully right. In audio mixing software, these physical pan pots are replaced by on-screen virtual knobs or sliders that function identically to their physical counterparts.
title: Panning (audio)

text: Panning is the process of adjusting the balance between stereo signals to reduce or reverse their width, allowing listeners to hear a single channel or a combined version of the left and right channels. This technique enables the separation of stereo channels to create a dual mono signal by sending the audio equally to both the left and right outputs of a mixer, effectively converting a stereo source into a mono format.
title: Panning (audio)

text: A market economy is an economic system where decisions regarding investment, production, and distribution are based on the interplay of supply and demand, which determines the prices of goods and services. The major defining characteristic of a market economy is that investment decisions, or the allocation of producer goods, are primarily made through capital and financial markets, contrasting with a planned economy where such decisions are embodied in an integrated state plan.
title: Market economy

text: By August 1945, the United States Army Air Forces' 509th Composite Group operated a specialized Silverplate version of the Boeing B-29 Superfortress to deliver atomic weapons from Tinian in the Mariana Islands. Following orders issued on July 25 for use on four Japanese cities, the first device was dropped on August 6. This Little Boy uranium gun-type bomb struck Hiroshima, while three days later on August 9, another B-29 delivered a Fat Man plutonium implosion-type bomb to Nagasaki. The immediate devastation caused by these weapons led to the deaths of 90,000–146,000 people in Hiroshima and 39,000–80,000 in Nagasaki, with approximately half of the fatalities occurring on the first day of the attacks.
title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

text: The mammalian sperm cell comprises a head, neck, midpiece, and tail. While the head houses the nucleus and the tail performs propulsion, the midpiece is specifically defined by a central filamentous core surrounded by many mitochondria spiralled around it. These organelles are essential for generating the ATP required to power the sperm's journey through the female reproductive tract.
title: Sperm

text: In animals, the majority of the energy required for sperm motility comes from the metabolism of fructose found in the seminal fluid. This biochemical process occurs within the mitochondria situated in the sperm's midpiece, which is positioned at the base of the sperm head. Consequently, these cells rely on this specific location to generate the necessary power for movement toward the egg, a function that cannot be reversed due to the mechanism of their propulsion.
title: Sperm

text: An equilateral triangle stands out as the most symmetrical shape, possessing exactly three lines of reflectional symmetry and a rotational order of three around its central point. text: Sharecropping is an agricultural system where landowners permit tenants to cultivate their fields, with the tenant receiving a share of the harvest in exchange for the land. While some arrangements are based on tradition, others are established through legal contracts, such as the Italian system of mezzadria, the French method of métayage, the Spanish practice of mediero, or the Islamic framework of muqasat, which are all documented in historical records.
title: Sharecropping

text: The Dragon Boat Festival, also known as the Duanwu Festival, is a traditional holiday originating in China that occurs near the summer solstice. It is also known as Zhongxiao Festival (Chinese: 忠孝節; pinyin: Zhōngxiàojié), commemorating fealty and filial piety. The festival now occurs on the 5th day of the 5th month of the traditional Chinese calendar, which is the source of the festival's alternative name, the Double Fifth Festival.[1] The Chinese calendar is lunisolar, so the date of the festival varies from year to year on the Gregorian calendar. In 2016, it occurred on June 9; and in 2017, on May 30.

text: Athens emerged as the dominant economic power in Greece around the late 6th century BCE, a period marked by the discovery of silver veins in the neighboring mountains that significantly boosted their wealth. This economic strength was further enhanced by an efficient trading system with other Greek city states. Archaeological evidence shows that over 80,000 amphorae and other goods were recovered from digs around Athens, indicating a massive trade volume. Additionally, marble and bronze artwork were traded, though this luxury trade only truly exploded after the rise of the Roman Republic. Despite poor soil conditions that forced Athens to import grain, the city remained a central hub for economic activity during this era.
title: Economic history of Greece and the Greek world

text:
Waivers (NHL)
After a player has been designated for assignment, the other 30 NHL teams can put in a claim or waive their claim for that player. The claims process starts at noon Eastern Time and ends 24 hours later. If only one team makes a claim for the player, then he will be transferred to the claiming team. If more than one team makes a claim, then the player will be transferred to the team having the lowest percentage of possible points in league standings at the time of the request for waivers. When a waiver claim has been secured, the claiming team must pay a transfer fee to the original club, though this fee is not counted against the salary cap. If waivers are requested outside the playing season, or before November 1, then the player shall be transferred to the team with the lowest points in the preceding season.

The claims process for NHL waivers begins at noon Eastern Time and concludes after 24 hours. If a single team secures a waiver claim, the player is transferred to that team.
title: Waivers (NHL)

When John Gilbert discovered Anna still lying in the building with the other vampires, he staked her, and her body was then burned with the others. Damon witnessed this and later informed Jeremy of her death, regretting that he could not have intervened. Jeremy later questioned if being a vampire would be preferable to Damon, who admitted that turning emotions off would be easier. text: The Articles of Confederation and Perpetual Union established the first constitution of the United States, serving as an agreement among the 13 original states that defined the nation's initial framework. Approved by the Second Continental Congress on November 15, 1777, this document was sent to the states for ratification, with the federal government gaining only powers previously recognized by the colonies. Although the federal authority came into force on March 1, 1781, after all 13 states ratified the document, a core guiding principle of the agreement was to preserve the independence and sovereignty of the states. Ultimately, the federal government remained weak, receiving only those powers that the colonies had explicitly acknowledged as belonging to the king and parliament.
title: Articles of Confederation

text: The New England Patriots have appeared in the Super Bowl ten times in franchise history, the most of any team. The team has since become one of the most successful franchises in NFL history, winning 15 AFC East titles in 17 seasons since 2001 without a single losing season. Notable achievements include the most wins in a ten-year period (126, in 2003–2012), an undefeated 16-game regular season in 2007, the longest winning streak in NFL history (21 games from October 2003 to October 2004), and the most consecutive division titles won by a team (nine straight from 2009 to 2017). The franchise owns the record for most Super Bowls reached (eight) and won (five) by a head coach–quarterback tandem. Currently, the Patriots are tied with the 49ers and Cowboys for the second most Super Bowl wins with five, trailing only the Steelers, who have six.

text: The Bank of England 10s note was a banknote of the pound sterling, where ten shillings in pre-decimal money was equivalent to half of one pound. This ten-shilling note was the smallest denomination note ever issued by the Bank of England and was first printed in 1928, continuing to be produced until 1969. The note ceased to be legal tender in 1970 and was subsequently removed in favor of the fifty pence coin.
title: Bank of England 10s note

text: A new design for ten-shilling notes was introduced in 1961, with the old notes ceasing to be legal tender in 1962. These series C notes were slightly longer and narrower than earlier versions, though they did not feature a portrait of Queen Elizabeth II on the front; instead, the reverse design incorporated the Bank of England logo. In the late 1960s, it was decided that future banknotes should feature a British historical figure on the reverse, leading to the first such ten-shilling note being introduced in 1970, which featured William Shakespeare. Only a design for a ten-shilling note featuring Walter Raleigh was approved in 1964, but it was never issued. Rather than replacing the paper notes, a new fifty pence coin was introduced in 1969 as part of the decimalisation process. The principal reason for this change was economy, as notes had an average lifetime of about five months whereas coins could last at least fifty years. Consequently, the series C ten shilling notes ceased to be legal tender on 22 November 1970, marking the end of their circulation.
title: Bank of England 10s note

text: The Golden State Warriors are an American professional basketball team based in the San Francisco Bay Area. While the league's Western Conference Pacific Division is the primary division they compete in, their success history is defined by five NBA championships won in 1947, 1956, 1975, 2015, and 2017. These five titles are tied for the fourth-most in NBA history, a record shared with the San Antonio Spurs.
title: Golden State Warriors

text: During the first half of the twentieth century, John B. Watson established the foundations of modern behaviorism by advocating for a scientific approach that rejected introspection in favor of studying only observable actions. Although Watson and Ivan Pavlov focused on classical conditioning, the philosophy of radical behaviorism was solidified in the 1930s when B. F. Skinner argued that private mental events must be subject to the same experimental controls as behavior, a theory that later evolved into operant conditioning.
title: Behaviorism

text: Since at least the mid-19th century, various concepts for a union among Canada, Mexico, and the United States of America have been proposed, including the North American Technate. Following the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and the Maastricht Treaty, speculation arose regarding the creation of a North American Union, a model similar to the European Union established by Maastricht, as a potential future step for the region.[12][13][14] Several proposals for continental integration of North America advocated for a union styled after the European Union, though many academic and business groups favored less dramatic changes involving the formation of a customs union or common market.[15][16]
title: North American Union

text: The Ranjit Sagar Dam, also known as the Thein Dam, is a hydroelectric project constructed by the Government of Punjab on the Ravi River, which forms the border between Jammu and Kashmir and Punjab. Situated near Pathankot city in Punjab, the dam is located adjacent to Kathua city and Basholi tehsil in Kathua district of J&K. This project is the largest hydroelectric dam of the state of Punjab, with the site township named Shah pur Kandi Township. Feasibility studies for the project began in 1953, and geotechnical studies continued until 1980. Construction commenced in 1981, when the generators were commissioned in 2000, and the project was completed in March 2001.
title: Ranjit Sagar Dam

text: In the legendarium of J. R. R. Tolkien, Valinor serves as the realm of the Valar located in Aman, and it is also known by the name of the Undying Lands, alongside Tol Eressëa and other outliers of the land. While this latter designation is somewhat misleading because the blessed land itself did not grant mortals eternal life, only immortal beings were generally permitted to reside there. Notably, the surviving bearers of the One Ring were allowed to dwell in Valinor for a time, including Bilbo and Frodo Baggins, Sam Gamgee, and perhaps Gimli.
title: Valinor

text: The title "Valinor" serves as the primary context for the following passage, which details the destination of the Elves: "After the destruction of Númenor, the Undying Lands were removed from Arda so that Men could not reach them. The Elves could go there only by the Straight Road and in ships capable of passing out of the spheres of the earth."
title: Valinor

text: Born on April 20, 1969, Felix Baumgartner is an Austrian skydiver and BASE jumper renowned for his daring feats. Best known for his historic jump from a helium balloon into the stratosphere on October 14, 2012, he shattered world records for skydiving an estimated 39 kilometers (24 miles), reaching a top speed of 1,357.64 kilometers per hour (843.6 miles per hour) or Mach 1.25. This descent marked the first time a person broke the sound barrier without vehicular power relative to the surface, while also setting records for exit altitude, vertical freefall distance without a drogue, and vertical speed without a drogue. Although he still holds the vertical speed record, the vertical freefall distance record was surpassed two years later by Alan Eustace on October 24, 2014.
title: Felix Baumgartner

text: Hospice care in the United States is often delayed until physicians are absolutely certain of a terminal prognosis, with some believing a six-month prognosis or less is required. Although the term of care continues to be underused, the average length of stay in hospice before a patient died was 26 days in 1994 and 19 days in 1998. In 2004, the average stay was 57 days and the median length was 22 days, with 33% of hospice patients admitted in 2004 dying within seven days of admission.
title: Hospice care in the United States

text: Calpurnia, nicknamed Cal, is the Finch family's African-American housekeeper, whom the children love and Atticus deeply respects. She is an important figure in Scout's life, providing discipline, instruction, and love. Calpurnia is a mother herself and raised her son, Zeebo, to adulthood. She also fills the maternal role for the children after their mother's death. Calpurnia is one of the few black characters in the novel who is able to read and write, and it is she who taught Scout to write. She learned how to read from Miss Maudie's aunt, Miss Buford, who taught her how to read out of Blackstone's Commentaries, a book given to her. Aunt Alexandra despised Calpurnia because Alexandra believed that Calpurnia was not a "maternal figure" for Jem and Scout, especially for Scout.
title: List of To Kill a Mockingbird characters

text: Lula is an African-American woman who harbors a dislike for white people, yet she is overruled by other congregants when Calpurnia attempts to bring Atticus Finch's children, Jem and Scout, to church. According to James Zeebo, Calpurnia's son, Lula's said to be, "a troublemaker from way back, with fancy ideas and haughty ways." She faces the threat of being "churched" (subjected to church discipline) by Reverend Sykes.
title: List of To Kill a Mockingbird characters

text: Zeebo, the eldest son of Calpurnia, stands as one of the only four individuals in First Purchase Church who possess the ability to read. This unique skill allows him to act as the vocal leader, guiding the congregation by reciting verses and prompting the rest of the members to repeat the lines. Calpurnia was the one who taught Zeebo how to read, and he is also recognized as the garbage collector of Maycomb, having removed the dead rabid dog, Tim Johnson. When a fellow church member, a woman named Lula, attempted to make the children feel bad for attending church with his mother, Zeebo welcomed Scout and Jem with open arms. He is described as kind but very quiet.
title: List of To Kill a Mockingbird characters

text: In the 2017 American League Championship Series, the Houston Astros emerged victorious as the home team, defeating the New York Yankees in seven games after falling behind three games to two.
title: 2017 American League Championship Series

text: By 1912, major motion-picture companies had set up production near or in Los Angeles.
title: Hollywood

text: The vasomotor center (VMC) is a specific section of the medulla oblongata that, alongside other vital centers, manages blood pressure and other homeostatic functions. Although the term "vasomotor center" is somewhat outdated, it describes a network of interacting neurons rather than a single isolated brain structure. When carbon dioxide levels rise at central chemoreceptors, this region stimulates the sympathetic system to constrict blood vessels, a mechanism that is reversed when carbon dioxide accumulates in tissues. The VMC receives input from cranial nerves IX and X, which are also critical for regulating blood pressure. The precise localization of this area was identified by Filipp Ovsyannikov in 1871.
title: Vasomotor center

text: Mexico competed in the Winter Olympics held from 9 to 25 February 2018, with four athletes participating across three sports.
title: Mexico at the 2018 Winter Olympics

text: While the earliest known written documentation of the Chinese abacus dates to the 2nd century BC, this specific artifact refers to a written record rather than the invention itself. The abacus, a tool for performing calculations, is believed to have originated in ancient China, with archaeological evidence suggesting its use began around the 2nd century BC.
title: Abacus

text: Ariana Clarice Richards (born September 11, 1979) is an American actress and painter who is best known for her role as Lex Murphy in the blockbuster film Jurassic Park.
title: Ariana Richards

text: In 1664, an English naval expedition under the command of Prince James, Duke of York, sailed into New Amsterdam harbor. Facing defeat, Director-General Peter Stuyvesant surrendered the settlement, which was subsequently renamed New York. This English takeover also resulted in the renaming of Fort Albany and the division of the region between the Hudson and Delaware rivers into New Jersey.
title: Dutch colonization of the Americas

text: While the Dutch briefly held parts of the North American continent during the Third Anglo-Dutch War between 1673 and 1674, they immediately returned these territories to England upon the signing of the Treaty of Westminster. Although Dutch Navy captain Jurriaen Aernoutsz temporarily seized forts in the French colony of Acadia in 1674, his appointed administrator John Rhoades lost command of the region after departing for Curaçao. Consequently, despite Aernoutsz's claims, Dutch sovereignty over this area remained nominal until the Netherlands formally surrendered its claim in the Treaties of Nijmegen.
title: Dutch colonization of the Americas

text: Article Two of the United States Constitution is the legal framework that defines the executive branch of the federal government, a body responsible for carrying out and enforcing federal laws. This branch encompasses the President, the Vice President, the Cabinet, executive departments, independent agencies, and other boards, commissions, and committees.
title: Article Two of the United States Constitution

text: The fifth season of the series consists of a double order of twenty episodes, split into two parts of ten episodes; the second half will premiere in 2018.
title: Vikings (season 5)

text: While the phrase is commonly attributed to Queen Marie Antoinette, there is no record of her having said it. Instead, the expression originates with Jean-Jacques Rousseau, who wrote it in the sixth book of his autobiography, *Confessions*. This work, which includes a passage recounting a theft of bread and wine, was published in 1782. In this context, the words were spoken by a "great princess" who had previously been described by Rousseau as an "elegantly dressed" figure.
title: Let them eat cake

text: In the developing B cell, the initial step of recombination involves joining a specific heavy-chain gene segment to a pre-existing DJ complex. This process occurs between one D and one J segment of the heavy chain locus, where any intervening DNA is deleted. Following this D-J recombination, one V gene segment is joined from a region upstream of the newly formed DJ complex, resulting in a rearranged VDJ gene segment. All other gene segments between V and D are subsequently deleted from the cell's genome. The primary transcript generated contains the VDJ region along with the constant mu and delta chains (Cμ and Cδ). Consequently, the primary RNA is processed to add a poly-A tail after the Cμ chain and to remove the sequence between the VDJ segment and the constant gene segment. Translation of this mRNA ultimately leads to the production of the Ig M heavy chain protein.
title: V(D)J recombination

text: Sri Lanka is a constituent member of South Asia, a geographical region defined by the collective territories of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. This economic cooperation organisation, known as the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC), was established in 1985 and encompasses all eight nations comprising this part of Asia.
title: South Asia

text: Star Wars Battlefront II is an action shooter video game based on the Star Wars film franchise, released worldwide on November 17, 2017, for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and Microsoft Windows.
title: Star Wars Battlefront II (2017 video game)

text: The song "Gimme Some Lovin'" is credited to Terry Reid, but the version featured in the movie Days of Thunder is actually from The Spencer Davis Group. This track also appeared on Reid's 1991 solo album, The Driver, alongside an alternate version of "The Last Note of Freedom" with different lyrics, titled "The Driver (Part 2)".
title: Days of Thunder (soundtrack)

text: Although PCH advertises its sweepstakes along with magazine subscriptions, no purchase is necessary to enter or win. In 1995, PCH began the tradition of announcing winners of its $10 million prize just after the Super Bowl. As of 2012, $225 million in prizes have been distributed. Some of its larger prizes are for $5,000 a week for life, or $10 million. Prizes can also range from $1 Amazon gift cards to $2,500, $1 million or $3 million. The larger cash prizes are paid in installments, typically with a balloon payment at 30 years, reducing the present value of prizes to much less than their nominal values.
title: Publishers Clearing House

text: Ellen's Game of Games, also known as Game of Games and stylized as ellen's GAME OF GAMES is an American television game show that premiered on December 18, 2017. A special preview episode aired on December 18, 2017, with the official series premiere on January 2, 2018.
title: Ellen's Game of Games

text: RWBY is an ongoing American anime-styled web series created by Rooster Teeth Productions that premiered on July 18, 2013 on the Rooster Teeth website. Four seasons, referred to as "Volumes", have been released, with a fifth currently ongoing since its premiere on October 14, 2017. As of October 2017, 54 episodes, which are referred to as "Chapters", have been released.
title: List of RWBY episodes

text: The fifth Volume of RWBY premiered on October 14, 2017, a date first announced at the RTX Austin 2017 event. Episodes are released to Rooster Teeth FIRST members Saturdays at 10am CT, then to registered members the following Tuesday, and to the general public the following Saturday.
title: List of RWBY episodes

text: In 1943, a nine-year-old boy named Bruno grew up in Berlin during the height of World War II. While residing with his family in Berlin, he was moved to a camp known as Out-With, a place where prisoners wore distinctive striped pyjamas. This incident occurred during the war, a time when Bruno's family had to leave their homes due to the orders of the "Fury," a figure Bruno interpreted as a leader. Although Bruno initially feared the move, he soon discovered that the camp was located near Auschwitz. As he explored the wire fence surrounding the camp, he encountered Shmuel, a Jewish boy who shared his birthday with Bruno. Shmuel explained that his family was separated from his mother, but they remained together on the other side of the fence. Bruno and Shmuel became close friends, often sneaking food to Shmuel and watching him grow thinner. Eventually, Bruno realized that Shmuel's family was trapped inside a death camp, a fact that Bruno never fully understood at the time.
title: The Boy in the Striped Pyjamas

text: In 1865, William Chatterton Dix composed the Christmas carol "What Child Is This?" while recovering from a severe illness; this work emerged from his spiritual renewal as an insurance company manager. Although the lyrics were penned in Great Britain, the song gained widespread popularity in the United States today.
title: What Child Is This?

text: The 2017 season was the Eagles' most successful in franchise history, as they defeated the New England Patriots in Super Bowl LII to become champions.
title: 2004 Philadelphia Eagles season

text: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar won the most NBA Most Valuable Player awards, securing the title six times.
title: NBA Most Valuable Player Award

text: When director Steven Spielberg first proposed casting Harrison Ford for the role, Lucasfilm studios rejected the suggestion, citing Ford's prior involvement in Star Wars and American Graffiti. Although Lucas did not wish to see Ford become known as his "Bobby De Niro," the casting process ultimately resulted in Tom Selleck being selected to portray Indiana Jones. Shortly after this decision, pre-production commenced for the film Raiders of the Lost Ark. However, the production faced a significant obstacle when CBS refused to release Selleck from his ongoing contract with Magnum, P.I., forcing him to decline the role.
title: Indiana Jones

text: Based on the biblical account in 1 Kings, the construction of the temple began in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, which falls within the conventional timeframe of 970 to 931 BCE. Consequently, the building process commenced in the mid-10th century BCE.
title: Solomon's Temple

text: Earle Hyman (October 11, 1926 – November 17, 2017) was an American stage, television, and film actor who appeared on The Cosby Show as the character Cliff's father, Russell Huxtable.
title: Earle Hyman

text: Shalom (Hebrew: שָׁלוֹם shalom) is a Hebrew term that translates to peace, harmony, wholeness, and completeness. While it can denote a state of well-being or tranquility, the word is also frequently employed idiomatically to signify both a greeting and a farewell.
title: Shalom

text: Shalom is a term that can refer to either peace between two entities, particularly between man and God or between two countries, or to the well-being, welfare, or safety of an individual or a group of individuals. Stendebach and Ringgren write that a more thorough etymological analysis of Hebrew roots reveals that 'Lom was the basic root word for Shalom, and the word shalom is also found in many other expressions and names. Its equivalent cognate in Arabic is salaam, sliem in Maltese, Shlama in Syriac-Assyrian and sälam in Ethiopian Semitic languages from the Proto-Semitic root Š-L-M.
title: Shalom

text: Hermann Ebbinghaus, who is considered one of the first to chart the course of forgetting over time, collected data in 1885 to plot a forgetting curve. Today, we approximate forgetting with an exponential curve [3]:
title: Forgetting curve

text: In the Muppet Movie, the character Walter, who questions his identity as a human versus a Muppet, performs a solo act of whistling in the telethon's finale. This musical performance was executed by musician Andrew Bird.
title: Walter (Muppet)

text: Craig Brown guided Scotland to qualification for the 1998 FIFA World Cup, finishing as the best runners-up. Scotland were drawn against holders Brazil in the opening game of the World Cup, but the final match against Morocco ended in a 3–0 defeat. Scotland have not appeared at the World Cup since.
title: Scotland at the FIFA World Cup

text: Andrew Garfield stars as the main character in the 2016 biographical war drama film Hacksaw Ridge, which tells the story of Desmond Doss, an American pacifist combat medic who refused to carry or use firearms during World War II. This Seventh-day Adventist Christian became the first conscientious objector to receive the Medal of Honor for his extraordinary service above and beyond the call of duty during the Battle of Okinawa.
title: Hacksaw Ridge

text: Released in 1977, "How Deep Is Your Love" is a pop ballad and rap-based track written and recorded by the Bee Gees. It was ultimately used as part of the soundtrack to the film Saturday Night Fever. The single was released in September of that year and topped the Billboard Hot 100 on December 24, 1977, becoming the first of six consecutive US number-one hits. This song ended the 10-week reign of Debby Boone's "You Light Up My Life" and stayed in the Top 10 for a then-record 17 weeks. It is listed at number 22 on the 55th anniversary edition of Billboard's All Time Top 100.
title: How Deep Is Your Love (Bee Gees song)

text: Rust is an iron oxide, a typically red substance created when iron combines with oxygen while water or air moisture is present. This process involves several distinct forms, which can be identified by visual inspection or spectroscopy and occur under different conditions. The resulting material primarily consists of hydrated iron(III) oxides, specifically Fe2O3·nH2O, alongside iron(III) oxide-hydroxides such as FeO(OH) and Fe(OH)3.
title: Rust

text: Rust is another name for iron oxide, which occurs when iron or an alloy containing iron, such as steel, is exposed to oxygen and moisture for a long period of time. Over time, the oxygen combines with the metal at an atomic level, forming a new compound called an oxide and weakening the bonds of the metal itself. Although some people refer to rust generally as "oxidation," that term is much more general; although rust forms when iron undergoes oxidation, not all oxidation forms rust. Only iron or alloys that contain iron can rust, but other metals can corrode in similar ways.
title: Rust

text: The Continental Congress voted to adopt the Declaration of Independence on July 2, 1776. Although the delegates were divided early on as to whether to break from Crown rule, the second Continental Congress on July 2, 1776, passed a resolution asserting independence, with no opposing vote recorded. The Declaration of Independence was issued two days later declaring themselves a new nation: the United States of America.
title: Continental Congress

text: The Second Continental Congress convened on May 10, 1775, at Philadelphia's State House, passing the resolution for independence the following year on July 2, 1776, and publicly asserting the decision two days later with the Declaration of Independence. Thomas Jefferson of Virginia drafted the declaration, and John Adams was a leader in the debates in favor of its adoption. John Hancock of Massachusetts was the president during those debates.
title: Continental Congress

text: The RMS Titanic, a British passenger liner, sank in the North Atlantic Ocean on the early morning of April 15, 1912, after colliding with an iceberg during its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York City. The vessel carried an estimated 2,224 passengers and crew, resulting in a death toll exceeding 1,500, which made it one of the deadliest commercial peacetime maritime disasters in modern history. Built by the Harland and Wolff shipyard in Belfast, the ship was the largest afloat at the time of its service and the second of three Olympic-class ocean liners operated by the White Star Line. Thomas Andrews, the ship's architect, perished in the disaster.
title: RMS Titanic

text: The Lincoln Highway was one of the earliest transcontinental highways for automobiles across the United States of America. Conceived in 1912 by Indiana entrepreneur Carl G. Fisher and formally dedicated on October 31, 1913, the route ran coast-to-coast from Times Square in New York City westward to Lincoln Park in San Francisco. Originally traversing 13 states, the highway passed through New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Iowa, Nebraska, Colorado, Wyoming, Utah, Nevada, and California. In 1915, the "Colorado Loop" was removed, and in 1928, a realignment relocated the route through the northern tip of West Virginia. Consequently, the highway eventually passed through a total of 14 states, 128 counties, and over 700 cities, towns, and villages.
title: Lincoln Highway

text: While most historians agree that conflicts over slavery caused the war, they disagree sharply regarding which kinds of conflict—ideological, economic, political, or social—were most important. The immediate catalyst to the civil war was slavery.
title: Origins of the American Civil War

text: The immediate catalyst for the secession that ignited the American Civil War was the Southern political leadership's steadfast opposition to Northern antislavery efforts aimed at halting the expansion of slavery into new western territories. While some scholars attribute the subsequent formation of the Confederacy to white Southern nationalism, the primary driver for the North's rejection of secession remained the preservation of the Union itself, a stance rooted in American nationalism. Although the debate often centers on the specific motivations behind the southern states' decision to withdraw, the core issue remains the resistance to northern attempts to contain the spread of slavery.
title: Origins of the American Civil War

text: Once water enters the soil, it can remain there, move downward to the groundwater table, or eventually contribute to the process of runoff.
title: Infiltration (hydrology)

text: Muhammad Yunus, a Bangladeshi social entrepreneur and economist, is best known for co-founding Grameen Bank and pioneering the concepts of microcredit and microfinance in 1976. These financial tools provide loans to entrepreneurs who are too poor to qualify for traditional bank loans. In 2006, Yunus and the Grameen Bank were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, specifically recognized for their efforts through microcredit to create economic and social development from below. The Norwegian Nobel Committee highlighted Yunus's work, stating that "lasting peace cannot be achieved unless large population groups find ways in which to break out of poverty" and that he has demonstrated how even the poorest of the poor can work to bring about their own development.
title: Muhammad Yunus

text: In 1976, Muhammad Yunus conducted field visits to the impoverished households in Jobra, a village near Chittagong University, where he observed that modest loans could yield significant returns for the poor. Specifically, village women who crafted bamboo furniture were forced to borrow from lenders at usurious rates to purchase raw materials, and they had to return the principal plus interest to the lenders. Traditional banks declined to offer such small, reasonable loans to the poor due to perceived high risks of default. However, Yunus argued that if given the opportunity, the poor would repay the funds, making the microcredit model a viable business strategy. As proof of this concept, Yunus lent US$27 to 42 women in the village, who each generated a profit of BDT 0.50 (US$0.02) on their loans. Consequently, Yunus is widely credited with formulating the idea of microcredit.
title: Muhammad Yunus

text: World Consumer Rights Day is observed annually on 15 March, a date celebrated by Consumers International to highlight critical issues such as ensuring access to fair internet access for those still offline, combating fraud, and improving online consumer protection.
title: Consumers International

text: A compression release engine brake, frequently known as a Jake Nett brake or Jacobs brake, functions as an engine braking mechanism installed on certain diesel engines. When activated, this device opens exhaust valves within the cylinders following the compression cycle, allowing trapped compressed air to escape and thereby slowing the vehicle.
title: Compression release engine brake

text: Puff, the Magic Dragon is a song written by Leonard Lipton, Peter Yarrow, and David Wintour that has been widely interpreted as a metaphor for the hardships of growing older, a meaning explicitly stated by Peter Yarrow as having no relationship to drug-taking.
title: Puff, the Magic Dragon

text: The First Battle of Bull Run, also known as the First Battle of Manassas, was fought on July 21, 1861, in Prince William County, Virginia, just north of the city of Manassas and about 25 miles west-southwest of Washington, D.C. It was the first major battle of the American Civil War. The Union's forces were slow in positioning themselves, allowing Confederate reinforcements time to arrive by rail. Each side had about 18,000 poorly trained and poorly led troops in their first battle. It was a Confederate victory, followed by a disorganized retreat of the Union forces.
title: First Battle of Bull Run

text: The economy of the Ming dynasty (1368–1644) of China was the largest in the world during that period, a status considered one of China's three golden ages alongside the Han and Song periods. While this era saw the increasing political influence of merchants and technological advancements, it was also characterized by the gradual weakening of imperial rule, a trend that ultimately led to the decline of the monarchy.
title: Economy of the Ming dynasty

text: Andreas Vesalius (31 December 1514 – 15 October 1564) was a 16th-century Flemish anatomist, physician, and author of one of the most influential books on human anatomy, De humani corporis fabrica (On the Fabric of the Human Body). Often referred to as the founder of modern human anatomy, Vesalius was born in Brussels, which was then part of the Habsburg Netherlands, and served as professor at the University of Padua before becoming Imperial physician at the court of Emperor Charles V.
title: Andreas Vesalius

text: As a result of a 1991 referendum in Houston, the two-year term was amended so that elected officials can serve up to three terms until 2015, where the three term limit and two year terms were replaced with a two four-year terms. A mayor is elected for a four-year term, previously the mayor, controller, and councilmembers were elected to a two-year term prior to the November 3, 2015 city elections, and can be elected to as many as two consecutive terms. City council members, who also have a three-term limit, are elected from eleven districts in the city, along with five at-large council members, who represent the entire city. Term limits with the City of Houston are absolute - past elected officeholders are prohibited from campaigning for their former council positions (which includes the Mayor and City Controller). The current Mayor of Houston is Sylvester Turner.
title: Politics of Houston

text: The Siege of Corinth, also known as the First Battle of Corinth, was an American Civil War engagement that took place in Corinth, Mississippi. This month-long siege involved Union forces under Major General Henry Halleck, who commanded the attack against the city's Confederate occupants led by General P.G.T. Beauregard. The conflict concluded with the successful capture of the town by Federal troops.
title: Siege of Corinth

text: Article One of the United States Constitution requires that a Representative be at least 25 years old, must be an inhabitant of the state in which he or she is elected, and must have been a citizen of the United States for the previous seven years. There is no requirement that a Representative reside within the district in which he or she represents; although this is usually the case, there have been occasional exceptions.
title: Article One of the United States Constitution

text: While the Kansas City Chiefs faced the Tennessee Titans in the Wild Card round and suffered a close 22-21 defeat, Derrick Henry led the Titans in rushing for 156 yards, securing the win that extended their NFL record for most consecutive home playoff losses to six.
title: Kansas City Chiefs

text: Hurricane Charley was the third named storm and the second major hurricane of the 2004 Atlantic season, reaching 150 mph (240 km/h) winds that classified it as a Category 4 storm on the Saffir-Simpson scale. It made landfall in southwestern Florida at its peak intensity, becoming the strongest hurricane to strike the United States since Hurricane Andrew in 1992.
title: Hurricane Charley

text: Hurricane Charley accelerated to the north-northeast, toward the southwest coast of Florida in response to the approach of an unseasonal mid-tropospheric trough. The storm rapidly intensified, strengthening from a 110 mph (180 km/h) hurricane with a minimum central barometric pressure of 965 mbar (hPa; 28.50 inHg) to a 145 mph (233 km/h) hurricane with a pressure of 947 mbar (hPa; 27.96 inHg) in just three hours. It continued to strengthen as it turned more to the northeast, and made landfall near the island of Cayo Costa, Florida as a 150 mph (240 km/h) Category 4 hurricane with a pressure of 941 mbar (hPa; 27.79 inHg) at approximately 1945 UTC on August 13. An hour later, the hurricane struck Punta Gorda as a 145 mph (233 km/h) storm and then passed up through Port Charlotte. However, the eye had shrunk before landfall, limiting the most powerful winds to an area within 7 mi (11 km) of the center.
title: Hurricane Charley

text: The starting five from each conference consists of three frontcourt players and two guards, selected by a combination of fan voting, player voting, and media voting. Fan voting is the primary method used to determine the composition of the all-star game, as seen in the 2017 league change where fan votes accounted for 50% of the total, alongside 25% from players and 25% from media.
title: NBA All-Star Game

text: Released in 1979, the Australian dystopian action film Mad Max, directed by George Miller, takes place in a future Australia where an unhinged policeman clashes with a savage motorcycle gang.
title: Mad Max

text: The film *Mad Max* initially received a polarized reception upon its release in April 1979, although it won three AACTA Awards and attracted a cult following, while its critical reputation has grown since. It earned more than US$100 million worldwide in gross revenue and held the Guinness record for most profitable film. Originally titled *Mad Max*, this title became the first in the series, giving rise to three sequels: *Mad Max 2* (1981), *Beyond Thunderdome* (1985), and *Fury Road* (2015).
title: Mad Max

text: Sympathetic nervous system stimulation triggers vasoconstriction in most blood vessels, including those in the skin, digestive tract, and kidneys, driven by norepinephrine from post-ganglionic neurons. However, this process is counterbalanced by beta-2 adrenergic receptors located throughout the body, which are stimulated by epinephrine released from the adrenal glands. These specific receptors in the skeletal muscles, heart, lungs, and brain facilitate blood shunting away from non-essential organs while boosting flow to vital structures during intense physical activity.
title: Sympathetic nervous system

text: In the opening verse of "People Are Crazy," a male narrator meets an elderly man in a bar, leading to the line where the old man declares, "God is great, beer is good / And people are crazy." The conversation continues through the second verse before they part ways, after which the narrator discovers in the paper that the deceased man was a millionaire who left his fortune to someone he barely knew. This revelation prompts the narrator to echo the line, "people are crazy." The song follows a 4/4 time signature in the key of F major, with Currington's vocals spanning from B♭3 to D5.
title: People Are Crazy

text: While the Qur'an advises Muslim women to dress modestly and cover their breasts and genitals, it does not mandate covering the head. This distinction is particularly noted regarding the wives of the Prophet, who are described as unique in their attire. In this context, the term "hijab" refers to a veil or scarf worn over the head, neck, and bosoms to fulfill the requirement for covering the head, a practice supported by various major Arab translations and dictionaries that interpret the Arabic phrase "over their bosoms" as requiring full head coverage.
title: Islam and clothing

text: Islamic dress in Europe, notably the variety of headdresses worn by Muslim women, has become a prominent symbol of the presence of Islam in western Europe. In several countries the adherence to hijab (an Arabic noun meaning "to cover") has led to political controversies and proposals for a legal ban. The Netherlands government has decided to introduce a ban on face-covering clothing, popularly described as the "burqa ban", although it does not only apply to the Afghan-model burqa. Other countries, such as France and Australia are debating similar legislation, or have more limited prohibitions. Some of them apply only to face-covering clothing such as the burqa, chador, boushiya, or niqab; some apply to any clothing with an Islamic religious symbolism such as the khimar, a type of headscarf. The issue has different names in different countries, and "the veil" or "hijab" may be used as general terms for the debate, representing more than just the veil itself, or the concept of modesty embodied in hijab.
title: Islam and clothing

text: The United States functions as a federal republic where the president, Congress, and federal courts collectively exercise powers designated for the national government under the Constitution. This structure establishes a system in which the federal government shares sovereignty with state governments.
title: Politics of the United States

text: The modern Democratic Party originated in the 1830s as a coalition of former factions within the Democratic-Republican Party, which had failed by 1824. title: History of the United States Democratic Party

text: The Environmental impact of aviation: In 1999, the contribution of civil aircraft-in-flight to global CO2 emissions was estimated to be around 2%. However, for high-altitude airliners that frequently fly near or in the stratosphere, non-CO2 altitude-sensitive effects may increase the total impact on anthropogenic climate change significantly. A 2007 report from the Environmental Change Institute / Oxford University posits a range closer to 4 percent cumulative effect.
title: Environmental impact of aviation

text: The Royal Mint is a government-owned mint that produces coins for the United Kingdom. Formed over 1,100 years ago, the mint was historically part of a series of mints that became centralised to produce coins for the Kingdom of England, all of Great Britain and eventually most of the British Empire. The original London mint from which the Royal Mint is the successor, was established in 886 AD and operated within the Tower of London for approximately 800 years before moving to what is now called Royal Mint Court where it remained until the 1960s. As Britain followed the rest of the world in decimalising its currency, the Mint moved from London to a new 38 acres (15Â ha) plant in Llantrisant, Wales where it has remained since.
title: Royal Mint

text: Work on the new Royal Mint began in August 1967 with the construction of a blank treatment plant and a striking plant. This first phase was officially opened on 17 December 1968 by the royal attendance of Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Philip, and their son Prince Charles. Originally, there were fears that the Royal family would face protests due to the Investiture of Prince Charles as the Prince of Wales, but such protests failed to materialise. The second phase of construction began in 1973 and included the addition of a means to mint coins from virgin metals, completing the full minting process. Upon completion, the final cost for the land, buildings, and plant came to £8 million. Coin minting and production gradually shifted to the new site over the next seven years until the last coin, a gold sovereign, was struck in London in November 1975. In an attempt to consolidate all previous coin-related acts, the Coinage Act of 1971 was passed, which among other things effectively abolished the individual role of Master of the Mint. Under this act, the Chancellor of the Exchequer took over the role, with a Deputy Master being appointed by the Treasury to exercise all the powers and duties of the Master within the mint.
title: Royal Mint

text: In publishing, art, and communication, content is the information and experiences that are directed towards an end-user or audience. Content is "something that is to be expressed through some medium, as speech, writing or any of various arts".

text: Content serves as the primary source of value for the end-user, encompassing both the data supplied via the medium and the manner in which it is conveyed. While the delivery channel itself offers little utility without the underlying information, communication scholar Marshall McLuhan famously defined the medium as the message. In this context, the specific method of information transmission significantly influences how the recipient perceives the content.
title: Content (media)

text: The initial unification of Upper and Lower Egypt occurred around 3000 BC, a time when the two distinct kingdoms maintained separate regalia. Ancient tradition identified Menes, likely the same individual as Narmer, as the architect of this merger. This historical event is vividly depicted on the Narmer Palette, where the king is shown wearing the Red Crown in one scene and the White Crown in another, symbolizing his rule over both lands.
title: Upper and Lower Egypt

text: Ashoka, the son of Bindusara, wanted to annex Kalinga with Magadha for commercial reasons, although some folktales indicate that he invaded for personal reason. Because Kalinga has many sea ports which Magadha lacks and Kalinga is between north and south part of India and main trade routes goes through it, Ashoka attacked Kalinga in 261 B.C. and a battle occurred between two armies near the river Daya. This site is now identified near Bhubaneswar, the capital city of Orissa. Although Ashoka was winner at the end of the day, the bloodshed and human suffering changed his mind forever.

text: In the United States and Canada, a political action committee (PAC) is a type of organization that pools campaign contributions from members and donates those funds to campaign for or against candidates, ballot initiatives, or legislation. This specific legal term has been established in the United States to support campaign finance reform, whereas other democracies utilize different terminology for units of political spending. At the federal level, an organization qualifies as a PAC when it receives or spends more than $1,000 for the purpose of influencing a federal election, a requirement detailed in the Federal Election Campaign Act as amended by the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act of 2002.
title: Political action committee

text: The Tiber (/ˈtaɪbər/, Latin Tiberis,[1] Italian Tevere, Italian pronunciation: [ˈteːvere])[2] is the third-longest river in Italy, rising in the Apennine Mountains in Emilia-Romagna and flowing 406 kilometres (252 mi) through Tuscany, Umbria and Lazio, where it is joined by the river Aniene, to the Tyrrhenian Sea, between Ostia and Fiumicino.[3] It drains a basin estimated at 17,375 square kilometres (6,709 sq mi). The Tiber has achieved lasting fame as the main watercourse of the city of Rome, which was founded on its eastern banks, making the named river the primary aquatic link associated with this ancient capital.
title: Tiber

text: Mount Whitney is the highest summit in the contiguous United States and the Sierra Nevada, standing at an elevation of 14,505 feet (4,421 m). Located on the boundary between California's Inyo and Tulare counties, this mountain is situated 84.6 miles west-northwest of the lowest point in North America, Badwater Basin, which sits 282 feet below sea level.
title: Mount Whitney

text: The former Presidents Act originally granted lifetime protection to former presidents, a provision that was later modified. Specifically, the 1997 amendment reduced this duration to ten years for those taking office after that year. However, the Former Presidents Protection Act of 2012 reversed this reduction. Consequently, all living former presidents and their spouses today are entitled to receive lifetime Secret Service protection.
title: Former Presidents Act

text: Former presidents received lifetime Secret Service protection from 1965 through 1996. Although a 1994 statute reduced post-presidential protection to ten years for those inaugurated after January 1, 1997, President Bill Clinton remained entitled to lifetime coverage under this law. Subsequent presidents were granted only ten years of protection. On January 10, 2013, President Obama signed the Former Presidents Protection Act of 2012, which reinstated lifetime protection for former presidents and their families, including George W. Bush and all future leaders.
title: Former Presidents Act

title: St. Albans Raid

text: Indian classical dance, also known as Shastriya Nritya, is a broad category of performance arts that originates from the religious Hindu musical theatre traditions found in ancient India. The theoretical framework and practical methods underlying these arts have their roots in the Sanskrit text Natya Shastra, as established by authoritative sources.
title: Indian classical dance

text: The Natya Shastra is the foundational treatise for classical dances of India, and this text is attributed to the ancient scholar Bharata Muni. Its first complete compilation is dated to between 200 BCE and 200 CE, though estimates vary between 500 BCE and 500 CE. The most studied version of the Natya Shastra text consists of about 6000 verses structured into 36 chapters. The text describes the theory of Tāṇḍava dance (Shiva), the theory of rasa, of bhāva, expression, gestures, acting techniques, basic steps, standing postures, all of which are part of Indian classical dances. Dance and performance arts are a form of expression of spiritual ideas, virtues and the essence of scriptures.
title: Indian classical dance

text: Chest pain is a frequent symptom for emergency medical services, and aspirin is the recommended treatment for patients with acute coronary syndrome who do not have recent serious bleeding. While supplemental oxygen was previously used for most individuals presenting with chest pain, it is no longer necessary unless oxygen saturation levels drop below 94% or signs of respiratory distress appear. Additionally, entonox is commonly employed by EMS staff in prehospital settings, though current evidence regarding its specific effectiveness remains limited.
title: Chest pain

title: California Aqueduct

text: The Canadian Shield, also known as the Laurentian Plateau or Bouclier canadien, is a vast area of exposed Precambrian igneous and high-grade metamorphic rocks that serves as the ancient geological core of North America. This region, which forms the North American Craton, is characterized by a deep bedrock structure stretching from the Great Lakes to the Arctic Ocean and covering more than half of the country. While the area features a thin layer of soil and sparse human population with minimal industrial development, it is notably defined by its prevalent mining industry.
title: Canadian Shield

text: The Canadian Shield is one of the world's richest areas in terms of mineral ores, filled with substantial deposits of nickel, gold, silver, and copper. Throughout the Shield, many mining towns extract these minerals, with Sudbury in Ontario being one of the largest and most well-known. This area is an exception to the normal process of forming minerals in the Shield because the Sudbury Basin is an ancient meteorite impact crater; ejecta from the meteorite impact was found in the Rove Formation in May 2007, and the nearby Temagami Magnetic Anomaly has striking similarities to the Sudbury Basin, suggesting it could be a second metal-rich impact crater.
title: Canadian Shield

text: Staind (/steɪnd/ STAYND) is an American rock band formed in 1995. The band's activity became more sporadic after their self-titled release; with Lewis pursuing a solo country music career and Mushok subsequently joining the band Saint Asonia, but the band continued to tour off and on in the coming years. As of 2016, Lewis had reiterated that the band has not broken up, and will possibly create another album, but that his current focus is his solo career. The band's most recently performed live in 2017, and as of 2018, is in a hiatus. The band has sold over 15 million records worldwide.[1] Many of the band's singles have substantially charted on US rock and all-format charts as well, including "It's Been Awhile", "Fade", "Price to Play", "So Far Away", and "Right Here".
title: Staind

text: The heart's electrical conduction system is responsible for transmitting signals that originate from the sinoatrial node to trigger heart muscle contractions. This pacemaking signal first spreads to the right and left atria, then proceeds through the atrioventricular node, the Bundle of His, and the bundle branches before reaching the ventricles. Consequently, the sequence of contraction begins with the atrial chambers, followed by the ventricular chambers, ensuring efficient pumping throughout the body.
title: Electrical conduction system of the heart

Kennedy delivered the lines "Ich bin ein Berliner" to emphasize the United States' unwavering support for West Germany, a sentiment that was particularly vital given that the Berlin Wall had been erected only two months prior to prevent East Germans from fleeing to the West.

title: Currencies of the European Union

text: The New Mexico whiptail (Cnemidophorus neomexicanus) is a female-only lizard species native to the southern United States, specifically New Mexico and Arizona, as well as northern Mexico in the state of Chihuahua. This reptile holds the distinction of being the official state reptile of New Mexico. It is one of several lizard species that reproduce solely through parthenogenesis, a form of reproduction where offspring are born without the need for a male partner. Individuals of this species may be created either by hybridizing the little striped whiptail with the western whiptail, or by the direct parthenogenic reproduction of an adult female.
title: New Mexico whiptail

text: New Mexico whiptails represent a unique case of reproductive strategy where interspecific hybridization occurs, yet the resulting offspring can reproduce independently through parthenogenesis. This mechanism allows the all-female population to evolve into a distinct species without the need for males, as the hybridization process prevents the formation of viable males while the parthenogenic ability ensures the lineage continues. This specific combination of hybridization and parthenogenesis serves as a key reproductive adaptation within the Cnemidophorus genus, including the New Mexico whiptail.
title: New Mexico whiptail

text: The New Mexico whiptail is a diurnal, insectivorous lizard found in semi-arid habitats such as grasslands, rocky areas, shrubland, and mountainside woodlands. This species reproduces through parthenogenesis, a process where up to four unfertilized eggs are laid in mid summer, and the resulting offspring hatch approximately eight weeks later.
title: New Mexico whiptail

text: The New Mexico whiptail lizard is a crossbreed of a western whiptail, which lives in the desert, and the little striped whiptail, which favours grasslands. This species is a female-only organism that reproduces exclusively through parthenogenesis, a form of asexual reproduction where an egg is produced without the need for a male partner. Although the lizard mates with other females of its own species to trigger ovulation, it does not require a male to lay eggs, as confirmed by the source text which states that despite reproducing asexually and being an all-female species, the whiptail still engages in mating behavior to stimulate egg production.
title: New Mexico whiptail

text: In the late 19th century, the major territorial scramble involving European imperial powers resulted in the occupation of most of the continent. While Egypt and Sudan were never formally incorporated into any of these empires, the British occupation of 1882 placed Egypt under effective British administration until 1922. Ultimately, this period of colonial dominance left only two fully independent states: Ethiopia (known to Europeans as "Abyssinia") and Liberia.
title: Africa

title: Confederate States Army

text: Acetate is the name for the polyatomic anion with the chemical formula CH3COO−, which is the conjugate base or ion typically found in aqueous solutions. This negatively charged ion is formed when acetic acid combines with an alkaline, earthy, or metallic base, and the simplest of these salts is hydrogen acetate, also known as acetic acid.
title: Acetate

title: Roman numerals

text: The general term for software designed to damage, disable, or steal data is Malware, short for malicious software. title: Malware

text: Milling is a machining process that removes material by performing many separate, small cuts. title: Milling (machining)

text: All Night Long (All Night) is a hit single by American singer-songwriter Lionel Richie from 1983. Taken from his second solo album, Can't Slow Down, it combined Richie's soulful Commodores style with Caribbean influences. This new, more dance music, pop-inspired approach proved popular, as the single reached number one on three Billboard charts (pop, R&B and adult contemporary).
title: All Night Long (All Night)

title: Howard Caine

text: Baez recounts a conversation with Bob Dylan that takes place in a 1960s hotel, where she reflects on a past relationship and the phrase "diamonds and rust" that serves as a metaphor for the cycle of love and loss.
title: Diamonds & Rust (song)

text: Matthew "Matt" Camden, the oldest brother of Annie and Eric, was played by Barry Watson. Born in 1980, Matt is the firstborn of Annie and Eric. In the beginning of the series, Matt is a junior in high school. He sacrifices his school time to help others; if they wished to remain anonymous, he would respect that and not even tell his father. During high school, he bounces from job to job, including tutor and Dairy Shack delivery driver. He is not always a star student, but he manages to graduate at the top of his class and get accepted for a White House internship in Washington, D.C. with First Lady Hillary Clinton. He returns to Glenoak for college, rooming with friend and fellow "P.K." John Hamilton. Matt's new uncle, Dr. Hank Hastings, helps him get a job in the hospital cafeteria; during his time there, he decides to become a doctor. He ends up working at a women's clinic with Hank, beginning by helping save the life of a woman who could not get anyone but Matt to take her symptoms of an ectopic pregnancy seriously.

text: Taylor Michel Momsen (born July 26, 1993) is an American singer, songwriter, former actress and model. text: In October 1898, the publication of The Turn of the Screw began, marking the novel's first appearance in serial format within Collier's Weekly magazine. This work, originally published in 1898 as a novella by Henry James, also made its debut in The Two Magics in New York City and London.
title: The Turn of the Screw

text: Authority is frequently used in government to describe the official power to act, yet it carries a distinct meaning from power itself. While power is simply the ability to influence others to perform actions they would not otherwise take, authority represents a legitimate claim to exercise that power. For instance, although a mob possesses the capacity to punish a criminal, only a court of law holds the authority to do so legally, as the law dictates.
title: Authority

text: The Caucasus Mountains are a mountain system located in West Asia that stretches between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea in the Caucasus region.
title: Caucasus Mountains

text: Edf Energy is an integrated energy company operating across the United Kingdom, where it manages 5.7 million customer accounts and provides electricity and gas services to both residential and commercial clients.
title: EDF Energy

text: Buffalo Lookout stands as the highest elevation within the Ozarks, situated within the Boston Mountains of Arkansas. This prominent peak serves as the definitive answer to inquiries regarding the region's summit, while the broader geological context of the area highlights the St. Francois Mountains as the core of the exposed dome.
title: Ozarks

text: In the 2002 young adult novel *Hoot*, the story unfolds in Florida, where the protagonist, Roy, encounters two peculiar friends and an antagonistic figure while attempting to halt the construction of a pancake house that would endanger a colony of burrowing owls residing on the property.
title: Hoot (novel)

text: Roy Eberhardt, the protagonist of the novel *Hoot*, relocates to Florida and settles into Coconut Cove, a town where his high school classmate Dana Matherson begins bullying him. On a school bus ride, Roy witnesses a boy running barefoot outside and attempts to exit the vehicle, only to be violently choked and strangled by Dana. After punching Dana in the face and breaking her nose, Roy manages to escape the bus. However, he is unable to pursue the fleeing boy, as a golf ball strikes him in the head. Consequently, the school suspends Roy from the bus for two weeks and mandates that he compose an apology letter to Dana, though Roy later initiates a truce that Dana refuses to acknowledge.
title: Hoot (novel)

text: Japan operates as a constitutional monarchy, a system where the Emperor's authority is strictly confined to ceremonial functions, leaving actual governance to a legislative and executive branch alongside a judicial system. This arrangement ensures that the nation's political power remains distinct from the symbolic role of the head of state.
title: Government of Japan

text: The Shot Heard Around the World, historically referred to as the Battle of Lexington and Concord, marks the first organized American military engagement where the first shots were fired by Americans acting under orders.
title: Shot heard round the world

text: Crowne Plaza is a multinational chain of full service, upscale hotels catering to business travelers and the meetings and conventions market. It forms part of the InterContinental Hotels Group family of brands, which also include InterContinental Hotels & Resorts and Holiday Inn Hotels & Resorts. This group operates in 52 countries with more than 400 hotels, typically situated in city centers, resorts, coastal towns, or near major airports.
title: Crowne Plaza

text: In his final season of professional golf, the legend Mark O'Meara secured two major titles in 1998, including his 15th victory at The Masters. This resurgence in form, which reached a career best in the Official World Golf Ranking, was partly attributed to the inspiration gained from his friendship with Tiger Woods, the rising star of the era.
title: Mark O'Meara

text: The song "Hallelujah I Love Her So" originated with American musician Ray Charles, who penned and released the jazz and rhythm and blues piece in 1956 for Atlantic Records. This track later appeared on his self-titled debut LP issued the following year. Originally inspired by Ike Turner's 1953 hit "Get It Over Baby," the composition reached the peak position of number five on the Billboard R&B chart.
title: Hallelujah I Love Her So

text: Horrid Henry is the first book of the Horrid Henry series, published in 1994 and written by Francesca Simon and illustrated by Tony Ross.
title: Horrid Henry (book)

text: Nodding your head in a specific motion is classified as a gesture, where the head tilts back and forth along the sagittal plane. In many cultures, this action serves to indicate agreement, acceptance, or acknowledgment.
title: Nod (gesture)

text: The Suez Canal is an artificial sea-level waterway located in Egypt, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through the Isthmus of Suez. Constructed by the Suez Canal Company between 1859 and 1869, it was officially opened on November 17, 1869. The canal offers watercraft a shorter journey between the North Atlantic and northern Indian Oceans via the Mediterranean and Red seas by avoiding the South Atlantic and southern Indian oceans, in turn reducing the journey by approximately 7,000 kilometres (4,300 mi). It extends from the northern terminus of Port Said to the southern terminus of Port Tewfik at the city of Suez. Its length is 193.30 km (120.11 mi), including its northern and southern access channels. In 2012, 17,225 vessels traversed the canal (47 per day).
title: Suez Canal

text: Basketball courts vary in size depending on the governing body. While the National Basketball Association (NBA) specifies a standard measurement of 94 by 50 feet, the International Basketball Federation (FIBA) rules call for a smaller court measuring exactly 28 by 15 metres. Additionally, amateur basketball regulations allow for significant size differences. A critical feature of any basketball court is the three-point arc located at both ends, which determines point values for shots taken from inside or outside the line.
title: Basketball court

text: In the 2018 Sri Lankan local elections, the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna emerged as the leading party, securing the most seats and local authorities. This victory was achieved despite a turnout of approximately 70%, with the party led by former president Mahinda Rajapaksa avoiding major incidents of violence during the process.
title: Sri Lankan local elections, 2018

text: The 1967 single "Can't Take My Eyes Off You," credited to Frankie Valli, was a significant hit for the singer. While it earned a gold record and peaked at No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100, it was co-written by Bob Gaudio, a bandmate of Valli in The Four Seasons. This track marked Valli's biggest solo achievement before he topped the charts in 1974 with "My Eyes Adored You."
title: Can't Take My Eyes Off You

text: Lake Placid, New York, is one of only three venues in history to host the Winter Olympics twice, having participated in the 1932 and 1980 editions.
title: Lake Placid, New York

text: The expression "hot rod" first emerged in the late 1930s within southern California, where enthusiasts raced modified vehicles on dry lake beds northeast of Los Angeles under the regulations of the Southern California Timing Association (SCTA). This recreational activity gained significant momentum after World War II, especially in the state, as many returning veterans received technical training in military service. Additionally, the term likely refers to the era when bootleggers altered cars to evade revenue agents during Prohibition, and some law enforcement vehicles were also customized in response to these customs.
title: Hot rod

text: The Commander Kawas Manekshaw Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra case, which took place in 1959, was a significant Indian legal proceeding involving a Naval Commander accused of murder. Although the initial jury verdict declared the accused not guilty, the Bombay High Court overturned this and ordered a bench trial. This trial marked the final instance of a jury trial in India before the government abolished such trials in most cases. The case received extensive media attention and inspired various works, including the 1973 film *Achanak* and the 2016 film *Rustom*.
title: K. M. Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra

text: Carolyn Sue Jones[3] (April 28, 1930 – August 3, 1983)[1] was an American actress of television and film who played the role of Morticia Addams in the original black and white television series The Addams Family.
title: Carolyn Jones

text: The White Princess is an eight-episode series where the marriage of Henry VII and Elizabeth of York effectively ends the Wars of the Roses by uniting the houses of Lancaster and York. However, their mutual enmity and distrust—as well as the political plots of their mothers—threaten to tear both the marriage and the kingdom apart.
title: The White Princess (miniseries)

text: Pac-Man (stylized as PAC-MAN) is an arcade game developed by Namco that was first released in Japan in May 1980. It was created by Japanese video game designer Toru Iwatani and licensed for distribution in the United States by Midway Games, where it was released in October 1980.
title: Pac-Man

text: All cars in the Supercars Championship must be front-engined and rear-wheel drive, utilizing a 5.0-litre, naturally aspirated V8-engine equipped with electronic fuel injection. This specific engine design is capable of producing between 460 and 485 kW (620â€"650 bhp). While manufacturers are free to choose between using an engine based on their own lineup or a generic engine provided by V8 Supercars, both Ford and Holden use US-based racing engines with pushrod actuated valves and two valves per cylinder. Mercedes, Nissan, and Volvo use modified versions of their own engines, featuring hydraulic-lift valves and four valves per cylinder. All engines in this championship are electronically limited to 7,500 rpm and have a compression ratio of 10:1.
title: Supercars Championship

text: The International Space Station (ISS) is a large artificial satellite designed for human habitation, which is currently the largest human-made object in low Earth orbit. Although the initial component of the ISS entered orbit in 1998, the facility has grown to include pressurised modules, external trusses, solar arrays, and other components that have been launched by Russian Proton and Soyuz rockets alongside American Space Shuttles.
title: International Space Station

text: "Mean Old World" is a blues song recorded by American blues electric guitar musician T-Bone Walker in 1942. It has been described as the first important blues recordings on the electric guitar. Over the years it has been interpreted and recorded by numerous blues, jazz and rock and roll artists.
title: Mean Old World

text: An unsaturated fat is defined as a lipid characterized by the presence of at least one double bond within its fatty acid chain. This structural feature distinguishes it from saturated fats, which lack such bonds, and determines the degree of saturation: a monounsaturated fat possesses exactly one double bond, whereas a polyunsaturated fat contains two or more.
title: Unsaturated fat

text: The 2009 film Ghosts of Girlfriends Past, which adapts Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol, was shot in Massachusetts between February 19 and July 2008. Directed by Mark Waters and written by Jon Lucas and Scott Moore, the movie starred Matthew McConaughey, Breckin Meyer, Jennifer Garner, Lacey Chabert, and Michael Douglas. Released on May 1, 2009, the production took place in the state during the specified timeframe.
title: Ghosts of Girlfriends Past

text: Ghosts of Girlfriends Past was originally set up at Touchstone Pictures with Ben Affleck attached to play the lead character, but he opted out of the movie. It was primarily filmed at Castle Hill in Ipswich, Massachusetts, where the production team worked to capture the film's atmosphere. The movie was also the first pairing of Michael Douglas and Anne Archer since the 1987 hit thriller Fatal Attraction, although they shared no scenes together. Jennifer Garner and Christa B. Allen again appear together for the first time since 13 Going on 30 in 2004, and they again play the older and younger versions of the same character.
title: Ghosts of Girlfriends Past
