text: President James Madison created the Second Bank of the United States, a financial institution modeled on Alexander Hamilton's First Bank. This organization was chartered by the President in 1816 and began operations at its main branch in Philadelphia on January 7, 1817. By 1832, the bank had expanded to manage twenty-five branch offices nationwide.
title: Second Bank of the United States

text: The deuterocanonical books, derived from the Greek phrase meaning "belonging to the second canon," is a term adopted in the 16th century by the Roman Catholic Church to denote those books and passages of the Christian Old Testament, as defined in 1546 by the Council of Trent, that were not found in the Hebrew Bible. This terminology distinguished these texts from the protocanonical books, which comprised the books of the Hebrew canon, and from the apocryphal books, which were Jewish-origin texts known to some as scripture but deemed non-canonical by the Council.
title: Deuterocanonical books

text: The Pittsburgh Steelers hold the record for the most Super Bowl championships with six titles. While the New England Patriots, Dallas Cowboys, and San Francisco 49ers each won five Super Bowls, the Steelers remain the sole team to achieve this feat twice, having won the 1973 and 1979 Super Bowls. This accomplishment stands in contrast to other franchises that have lost more games than they have won, such as the Denver Broncos, who lost five Super Bowls, or the Buffalo Bills, who have lost four. The only team to win three out of four consecutive Super Bowls is the New England Patriots, who also hold the record for the most Super Bowl appearances with nine wins.
title: List of Super Bowl champions

text: The Chinese Immigration Act, 1923, was the legislation that finally passed, following years of pressure from federal and provincial governments to discourage Chinese immigration. Before this date, the country's immigration was heavily controlled by the earlier Chinese Immigration Act of 1885, which had imposed a hefty head tax on all immigrants from China. The new act went into effect on July 1, 1923, and it banned Chinese immigrants from entering Canada except those under specific titles.
title: Chinese Immigration Act, 1923

text: In plant anatomy, sieve tube elements, also known as sieve tube members, are highly specialized elongated cells found within the phloem tissue of flowering plants. These cells function as the primary conduits for transporting carbohydrates, mainly sucrose, from leaves to fruits and roots. A key distinction from water-conducting xylem vessel elements is that while xylem cells are dead upon maturation, sieve tube elements remain living. Furthermore, unlike xylem, sieve elements lack a nucleus at maturity, yet their ends are connected to one another, forming a continuous sieve tube.
title: Sieve tube element

text: The 2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament concluded its 80th edition on April 2 at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas.

text: Nine years later, a young boy named Sam queries his neighbor Beth about needing the lawn mowed. Beth suspects this boy, who lives with his "father" two blocks away, is actually her lost son, and as Sam mows the lawn, she takes photographs to show her husband and teenage son. The latter then confirms that he suspected the boy's true identity all along. When the parents contact Detective Candy Bliss, she offers cryptic and conflicting advice. It is learned that at the reunion in Chicago, the celebrity alumna Cecil Lockhart kidnapped Ben, renamed him Sam, and raised him as her own child until she was committed to a mental hospital, leaving Sam to be raised in a house only two blocks from the Cappadoras by his adoptive father, the sensitive and intellectual George Karras.
title: The Deep End of the Ocean

text: "...Baby One More Time" is the debut single by American singer Britney Spears, a song written by Max Martin and produced by Martin and Rami, and released in 1998 by Jive Records for Spears's debut album of the same name. This teen pop and dance-pop track refers to a girl's feelings after a break-up with her boyfriend.
title: ...Baby One More Time (song)

text: The black students gathered in the gymnasium to audition for the team, but the meeting turned into a fiasco when white students and Yoast interrupted. On August 15, 1971, the players journeyed to Gettysburg College, where their training camp took place. As the days of training camp progressed, black and white football team members frequently clashed in racially motivated conflicts, including some between captains Gerry Bertier and Julius Campbell. However, after forceful coaching and rigorous athletic training by Boone, which included an early morning run to the Gettysburg cemetery and a motivational speech, the team achieved racial harmony and success. After returning from football camp, Boone was told by a member of the school board that if he lost even a single game, he would be dismissed. Subsequently, the Titans went through the season undefeated while battling racial prejudice, before slowly gaining support from the community. Gerry even had his best friend Ray removed from the team because of his racism, following a game where he intentionally missed a block which consequently led to the near-season-ending injury of starting quarterback Jerry "Rev" Harris.
title: Remember the Titans

text: The New York City Subway is a rapid transit system that began operations in 1904, making it one of the world's oldest public transit systems.
title: New York City Subway

text: The Great Blizzard of 1888 helped demonstrate the benefits of an underground transportation system. A plan for the construction of the subway was approved in 1894, and construction began in 1900. The first underground line of the subway opened on October 27, 1904, almost 36 years after the opening of the first elevated line in New York City, which became the IRT Ninth Avenue Line. The fare was $0.05 and on the first day the trains carried over 150,000 passengers. The oldest structure still in use opened in 1885 as part of the BMT Lexington Avenue Line in Brooklyn and is now part of the BMT Jamaica Line. The oldest right-of-way, which is part of the BMT West End Line near Coney Island Creek, was in use in 1864 as a steam railroad called the Brooklyn, Bath and Coney Island Rail Road.
title: New York City Subway

He served as the Chief Minister of West Bengal from 1977 until 2000, a tenure that established him as the longest-serving Chief Minister in the nation's history. This political career spanned from his membership in the party's founding Politburo in 1964 until his death in 2010.
title: Jyoti Basu

text: The most runs ever scored in a single MLB inning is 18, a record set by the Chicago White Stockings (now the Cubs) against the Detroit Wolverines on September 6, 1883. While the modern-day record stands at 17, it was achieved by the Boston Red Sox against the Detroit Tigers on June 18, 1953.

text: Norman invaders established castles in England to serve defensive and pacifying functions. title: Castle

text: The Second Battle of El Alamein (23 October – 11 November 1942) was a major engagement during the Second World War that occurred near the Egyptian railway halt of El Alamein. This decisive victory by the Allies marked the turning point of the Western Desert Campaign, as it halted Axis advances into Egypt. The battle took place shortly after Lieutenant-General Sir Bernard Law Montgomery assumed command of the Eighth Army, following the sacking of General Claude Auchinleck and the death of Lieutenant-General William Gott in an air crash.
title: Second Battle of El Alamein

text: The Second Battle of El Alamein was fought in Egypt.
title: Second Battle of El Alamein

text: The concept of dementia as a normal part of aging was once held by ancient Greek and Roman thinkers, but it was not until 1901 that German psychiatrist Alois Alzheimer identified the first instance of this condition. He diagnosed a fifty-year-old woman named Auguste D., whose illness he tracked until her death in 1906, after which he publicly disseminated his findings in 1906. This breakthrough case marked the beginning of a five-year period during which eleven similar medical cases were documented, some of which already utilized the term Alzheimer's disease. Although Emil Kraepelin later formally described the disease as a distinct condition in 1910, he initially categorized it as a subtype of senile dementia.
title: Alzheimer's disease

text: The phrase "dressed to the nines" is said to be Scots in origin. The earliest written example of the phrase is from the 1719 Epistle to Ramsay by the Scottish poet William Hamilton, who used it in the context of his poem "To the nines."
title: To the nines

text: The Mercedes-Benz G-Class, often referred to as a G-Wagen (an abbreviation for the German term "cross country vehicle"), is a mid-size four-wheel drive luxury SUV produced by Magna Steyr, which was previously Steyr-Daimler-Puch, and is now sold by Mercedes-Benz in Austria. This vehicle is defined by its distinctive boxy styling and body-on-frame design, featuring three fully locking differentials—a rare trait among automobiles. Although an intended successor, the unibody Mercedes-Benz GL-Class, was introduced in 2006, the G-Class remains in active production today. It stands as one of the longest-running Mercedes-Benz models in the company's history, having been manufactured for a span of 35 years, a record that only the Unimog has surpassed.
title: Mercedes-Benz G-Class

text: American foreign policy after the onset of World War I was defined by a declaration of neutrality. This stance was maintained until the United States declared war in April 1917, a decision driven by the sinking of the RMS Lusitania and the broader realization that Germany's unrestricted submarine warfare threatened American civilians. Prior to this shift, American public opinion and the U.S. government largely adhered to neutrality, which allowed private corporations and banks to trade with either side without interference. However, as the war escalated, the U.S. eventually entered the conflict after the German military's failed spring offensive left them in a hopeless position, leading to a change in policy that began in 1917.
title: History of U.S. foreign policy

The film stars Owen Wilson and Jennifer Aniston as Marley's owners, while the movie was set to be released in the United States and Canada on December 25, 2008. text: The Mayflower featured a cabin for Master Christopher Jones on the main deck, measuring approximately ten by seven feet, situated aft in the stern. Forward of this cabin was the steerage room, which contained a whipstaff for sailing control rather than a wheel, along with the ship's compass and officer berths. text: A USB flash drive, also variously known as a thumb drive, pen drive, gig stick, jump drive, disk key, disk on key, flash-drive, memory stick or USB memory, is a data storage device that includes flash memory with an integrated USB interface. It is typically removable, rewritable and much smaller than an optical disc. Most weigh less than 30 g (1 ounce). Since first appearing on the market in late 2000, as with virtually all other computer memory devices, storage capacities have risen while prices have dropped. As of March 2016, flash drives with anywhere from 8 to 256 GB are frequently sold; less frequent are 512 GB and 1 TB units. Storage capacities as large as 2 TB are planned, with steady improvements in size and price per capacity expected. Some allow up to 100,000 write/erase cycles, depending on the exact type of memory chip used, and are thought to last between 10 and 100 years under normal circumstances (shelf storage time).

text: Players are currently inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum through election by either the Baseball Writers' Association of America (or BBWAA), or the Veterans Committee, which now consists of four subcommittees, each of which considers and votes for candidates from a separate era of baseball. Five years after retirement, any player with 10 years of major league experience who passes a screening committee is eligible to be elected by BBWAA members with 10 years' membership or more who also have been actively covering MLB at any time in the 10 years preceding the election. From a final ballot typically including 25 to 40 candidates, each writer may vote for up to 10 players; until the late 1950s, voters were advised to cast votes for the maximum 10 candidates. Any player named on 75% or more of all ballots cast is elected. A player who is named on fewer than 5% of ballots is dropped from future elections. In some instances, the screening committee had restored their names to later ballots, but in the mid-1990s, dropped players were made permanently ineligible for Hall of Fame consideration, even by the Veterans Committee. A 2001 change in the election procedures restored the eligibility of these dropped players; while their names will not appear on future BBWAA ballots, they may be considered by the Veterans Committee. Players receiving 5% or more of the votes but fewer than 75% are reconsidered annually until a maximum of ten years of eligibility.
title: National Baseball Hall of Fame and Museum

text: Acronym is the term used to describe initials that stand for something. Although the word acronym is often used to refer to any abbreviation formed from initial letters, some dictionaries and usage commentators define acronym to mean an abbreviation that is pronounced as a word, in contrast to an initialism (or alphabetism)—an abbreviation formed from a string of initials (and possibly pronounced as individual letters). The distinction, when made, hinges on whether the abbreviation is pronounced as a word or as a string of individual letters. Examples in reference works that make the distinction include NATO /ˈneɪtoʊ/, scuba /ˈskuːbə/, and radar /ˈreɪdɑːr/ for acronyms; and FBI /ˌɛfˌbiːˈaɪ/, CRT /ˌsiːˌɑːrˈtiː/, and HTML /ˌeɪtʃˌtiːˌɛmˈɛl/ for initialisms. title: Acronym

text: The geopolitical divisions in Europe that created a concept of East and West originated in the Roman Empire. While the Eastern Mediterranean was home to urbanized cultures using Greek as their common language, the West was characterized by a more rural landscape and the adoption of Latin. Following the fall of the Western Roman Empire, Western and Central Europe became separated from the East, where Byzantine Greek culture and Eastern Christianity became foundational influences for the Arab/Muslim world and among the Eastern and Southern Slavic peoples. Consequently, Roman Catholic Western and Central Europe maintained a distinct identity, especially as it began to redevelop during the Renaissance. Even after the Protestant Reformation, Protestant Europe continued to view itself as more closely tied to Roman Catholic Europe than other parts of the perceived civilized world.
title: Western world

The impeachment and subsequent trial were among the most dramatic events in the nation's political life, characterized by Johnson's defiance of an unconstitutional piece of legislation and conducted with little regard for the will of a general public that, despite the unpopularity of Johnson, opposed the impeachment.

text: In traditional Western notation, the scale used for a composition is typically indicated by a key signature at the beginning to designate the specific pitches comprising that scale. As the music advances, the pitches employed may shift, resulting in a different scale. Music can be transposed from one scale to another for various purposes, often to accommodate the range of a vocalist. Such transposition raises or lowers the overall pitch range while preserving the intervallic relationships of the original scale. For instance, transposition from the key of C major to D major raises all pitches of the C major scale equally by a whole tone. Since the interval relationships remain unchanged, transposition may go unnoticed by a listener, yet other qualities may change noticeably because transposition alters the relationship between the overall pitch range and the range of the instruments or voices performing the music. This often affects the music's overall sound, as well as having technical implications for the performers.
title: Music theory

text: In 1953, the United States Committee for UNICEF, later renamed the U.S. Fund for UNICEF, began actively promoting the program. By the 1960s, the initiative had spread across the United States, where small orange collection boxes were distributed to millions of trick-or-treaters. When UNICEF received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965, U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson acknowledged in his congratulatory letter that the "Trick or Treat Day" had transformed a holiday plagued by youthful vandalism into a program of basic training in world citizenship. In 1967, Johnson officially declared October 31 as "UNICEF Day," and by 1969, 3.5 million American children were participating in trick-or-treating to raise funds. Over the years, children and adults in the U.S. have collectively collected more than US $175 million for Trick-or-Treat for UNICEF, which supports UNICEF's global programing. Although donations are used to fund the organization's worldwide efforts, a significant portion of proceeds in 2005 was directed toward a domestic cause to aid victims of Hurricane Katrina. The campaign has evolved over time, with the U.S. Fund for UNICEF introducing mobile phone text message donations and a MySpace and Facebook page in 2008. Furthermore, in 2014, the U.S. Fund for UNICEF partnered with Crowdrise to expand the online presence of the campaign, enabling participants to build personal fundraising web pages alongside traditional door-to-door trick-or-treating.

text: The Saint of Killers is a character from the Preacher series who first appeared as a heartless murderer before being transformed into the Angel of Death, a role he assumes to collect the souls of those who die by violence. Following his reanimation, Heaven arranged for him to be put into a deep slumber until he was needed to kill people. The Saint was a primary antagonist in the Preacher series, tasked by Heaven to kill protagonist Jesse Custer due to his possession of the entity Genesis. Aside from Ennis and Dillon's Preacher, the Saint was featured in his own four-issue limited series, Preacher: Saint of Killers, which expanded on the Saint's background and motivation, and has appeared briefly in the DC Comics series Hitman, centered on a "wise-cracking assassin plying his trade in Gotham City". In the television series adaptation of Preacher, the Saint is portrayed by Graham McTavish.
title: Saint of Killers

text: April Ludgate traveled to Venezuela between seasons but returned to Pawnee to continue her job at the Parks Department. She eventually breaks up with Eduardo, a Spanish-speaking Venezuelan boyfriend, after he becomes friends with Andy, a man she was only used to make jealous. To prove her love for Andy, April tells him to do all the things she hates doing for her for a month. After only one day of him doing this, April kisses Andy. They decide to get married in "April and Andy's Fancy Party" after only one month of dating. Andy had proposed to April the day before the party asking, "What if we got married tomorrow?" to which April replied, "Fine." They were married at their dinner party (which was actually a surprise ceremony) in front of their friends and family.
title: April Ludgate

text: At the start of Season 6, April decides to pursue Veterinary School, an ambition she abandons upon meeting Ann. While she initially supported Andy's move to London, she was deeply distressed when he was away and missed him. Her relationship with Donna deepens, and together they attempt to stop Tom from leaving the Parks Department by becoming unhelpful as he seeks a property for his restaurant; eventually, they help him locate the ideal location. When Andy returns, April actively supports him in playing music for children, deciding to become his manager. Although she was excited that Ann was leaving Pawnee, the two share a nostalgic farewell at the Pawnee Commons site in "Ann and Chris." Along with Andy, Tom, and other Pawnee youths, they devise the idea for a Unity concert celebrating the merger. In the season finale, April names Leslie a founder of the revamped city of Pawnee, motivating her to convince the National Park Service to relocate the Midwest Branch to Pawnee, which enables Leslie and Ben to remain. Furthermore, it is revealed that April and Andy remain happily married in 2017, with April working for Leslie.
title: April Ludgate

text: In a series of flash-forwards at the conclusion of the final episode, April and Andy seek Leslie and Ben's advice on the prospect of having children, noting that Andy strongly desires this while April does not. They eventually decide to attempt conception, resulting in the birth of their son Jack on Halloween 2023. By 2025, the couple is expecting their second child.
title: April Ludgate

text: The Abolition of Corporal Punishment Act, 1997 (Act No. 33 of 1997) is an act of the Parliament of South Africa that abolished judicial corporal punishment, following the Constitutional Court's 1995 decision in the case of S v Williams and Others. Although the ruling in S v Williams was limited to the corporal punishment of males under the age of 21, Justice Langa mentioned in dicta that there was a consensus that corporal punishment of adults was also unconstitutional.
title: Abolition of Corporal Punishment Act, 1997

text: The Jamestown settlement, established as the first permanent English colony in the Americas, was founded on May 4, 1607, by the Virginia Company of London. While the British Empire is often cited as the starting point of the empire, the specific location of this initial North American presence is identified as Virginia, where the settlement became known as James Fort.
title: Jamestown, Virginia

text: The Bill of Rights, also known as the English Bill of Rights, is a significant Act of the Parliament of England that governs constitutional matters and establishes basic civil rights. This historical document received the Royal Assent on 16 December 1689, marking a pivotal shift in governance. It serves as a formal restatement of the Declaration of Right presented by the Convention Parliament to William III and Mary II in February 1689, which invited them to become joint sovereigns of England. The legislation lays down limits on the monarch's powers and explicitly sets out the rights of Parliament, including the requirement for regular parliaments, free elections, and freedom of speech within the legislature. Furthermore, it establishes certain individual rights such as the prohibition of cruel and unusual punishment and reestablished Protestants having the right to bear arms for their defense under the rule of law. Additionally, the document described and condemned several misdeeds committed by James II of England.
title: Bill of Rights 1689

text: Prince Edward Island (PEI or P.E.I.; French: Île-du-Prince-Édouard) is a province of Canada consisting of the island of the same name, and several much smaller islands. This small province is part of the traditional lands of the Mi'kmaq and was federated into Canada as a province in 1873, with Charlottetown serving as its capital. According to the 2016 census, the province of Prince Edward Island has 142,907 residents.
title: Prince Edward Island

text: Peter Andrew Beardsley MBE, born on 18 January 1961, is an English footballer who played as a forward or midfielder between 1979 and 1999. He notably represented his country 59 times between 1986 and 1996, serving as captain during the 1986 and 1990 FIFA World Cups and participating in UEFA Euro 1988. In club life, Beardsley played for Manchester United, Manchester City, and Everton, among other teams, having also been linked with spells with Newcastle United, Liverpool, Vancouver Whitecaps, Bolton Wanderers, Hartlepool United, and the Melbourne Knights. He was briefly appointed caretaker manager of Newcastle United in 2010.
title: Peter Beardsley

The Packers' starting quarterback for the 2016 season was Aaron Rodgers, who was playing in his 12th season in the NFL. They are listed in order of the date of each player's first start at quarterback for the Packers.
title: List of Green Bay Packers starting quarterbacks

text: The Tower of London, officially Her Majesty's Royal Palace and Fortress of the Tower of London, is a historic castle located on the north bank of the River Thames in central London. It lies within the London Borough of Tower Hamlets, separated from the eastern edge of the square mile of the City of London by the open space known as Tower Hill. It was founded towards the end of 1066 as part of the Norman Conquest of England. The White Tower, which gives the entire castle its name, was built by William the Conqueror in 1078 and was a resented symbol of oppression, inflicted upon London by the new ruling elite.
title: Tower of London

text: The United States Constitution is the supreme law of the United States. Originally comprising seven articles, it delineates the national frame of government. Its first three articles entrench the doctrine of the separation of powers, whereby the federal government is divided into three branches: the legislative, consisting of the bicameral Congress; the executive, consisting of the President; and the judicial, consisting of the Supreme Court and other federal courts.
title: United States Constitution

text: The highest court in each district is that of the District and Sessions Judge, which serves as the principal court of original civil jurisdiction alongside the High Court of the State. This court derives its civil authority from the Code of Civil Procedure and functions as a court of Sessions for criminal matters under the Code of Criminal Procedure. The District Judge presiding over this court is appointed by the state Governor with the advice of the state chief justice, while Additional District Judges and Assistant District Judges may also serve depending on the workload.
title: District Courts of India

text: While it is generally accepted that sustainable gray wolf packs were eradicated from Yellowstone by 1926, a 1975–77 study revealed that sightings of wolves in the park persisted during the period 1927 to 1977. The National Park Service continued its predator control policies until 1933, after which reliable sightings were observed between 1977 and the re-introduction in 1995, with these events most likely involving solitary or paired wolves transiting the region.
title: History of wolves in Yellowstone

text: In United States federal courts, the term currently applies solely to cases brought under diversity jurisdiction, meaning the court can hear the case only because it is between citizens of different states. Under Section 1332(a) of the United States Code, the United States Congress has decreed that such suits may proceed only where the matter in controversy exceeds the sum or value of $75,000. This figure represents a significant increase from earlier years.
title: Amount in controversy

text: Bacteroides fragilis is an obligately anaerobic, Gram-negative, rod-shaped bacterium that is part of the normal flora of the human colon and is generally commensal, although it can cause infection if displaced into the bloodstream or surrounding tissue following surgery, disease, or trauma.
title: Bacteroides fragilis

text: While the song "Rock and Roll All Nite" was originally released as the A-side of the 1975 album *Dressed to Kill*, it was originally performed by the band Kiss. The studio version of this track peaked at No. 68 on the Billboard singles chart, surpassing their previous hit "Kissin' Time." Although a live single from October 1975 reached No. 12 in early 1976, the song is best known as the group's signature track, which has served as their closing concert number in almost every performance since 1976. Additionally, in 2008, VH1 named it the 16th greatest hard rock song of all time.
title: Rock and Roll All Nite

text: Hellenism (religion), also known as Hellenic Polytheism or Dodekatheism, refers to various religious movements that revive or reconstruct ancient Greek religious practices, publicly emerging since the 1990s.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: Hellenism is the most common term used by modern adherents to identify the polytheistic religion, though it can also refer to the ancient Greek religion and culture. This concept originally stems from a systematization and revival of Greek religion done by the Roman Emperor Julian, who used the term to describe traditional Greek religion. Additionally, subgroups often employ various names to distinguish specific schools of thought or modern traditions, and the terms Hellenic religion and Hellenic polytheism are used interchangeably to refer to the same faith.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: Hellenism is a term used to describe the religion of the Greek gods, which is practiced by the Hellenic polytheist organization Hellenion. This group identifies its practices as "Hellenic Pagan Reconstructionism" and uses the term "Hellenismos" (Ἑλληνισμός, Hellēnismós) to describe the religion.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: Hellenism is a devotional or votive religion primarily based on the exchange of gifts (offerings) for the gods' blessings, where Hellenic polytheists honor both physical and spiritual ancestors. This tradition is characterized by ethical convictions inspired by ancient Greek virtues such as reciprocity, hospitality, self-control, and moderation, often guided by moral codes like the Delphic maxims or Aristotle's Ethics. A central concept in this system is kharis (or "charis", grace), which establishes reciprocity between humanity and the gods, while another key value is eusebeia, implying a commitment to the worship of the Hellenic gods backed by action.
title: Hellenism (religion)

text: A lacteal is a specialized lymphatic capillary responsible for absorbing dietary fats within the villi of the small intestine.
title: Lacteal

text: Lacteals are the specific lymphatic vessels located within the small intestine. These vessels function as the primary transport route for dietary fats, receiving chylomicrons formed in the enterocytes. As these lipoprotein particles pass through the lacteals, they combine with other components to create a milky substance known as chyle. The lacteals subsequently merge to form larger lymphatic vessels that carry the chyle to the thoracic duct, which empties it into the bloodstream at the subclavian vein.
title: Lacteal

text: The Parthenon's inner sanctuary, specifically the cella, served as the residence for the chryselephantine statue of Athena Parthenos, a work sculpted by Phidias and dedicated around 439 or 438 BC. This temple was originally dedicated to the goddess Athena, though construction extended until nearly the start of the Peloponnesian War in 432 BC. By the year 438, the sculptural decoration of the Doric metopes on the frieze above the exterior colonnade and the Ionic frieze surrounding the upper walls of the cella had been finished. Additionally, the opisthodomus, the back room within the cella, held the monetary contributions of the Delian League, which was led by Athens.
title: Parthenon

text: The Parthenon's inner sanctuary, or naos, is where the famous statue of Athena resides. Although this massive chryselephantine sculpture by Phidias is now lost, it was once housed within this sacred chamber and is known only through copies, vase paintings, gems, and literary descriptions.
title: Parthenon

text: Born Leland Michael Postil on September 29, 1944, Mike Post is an American composer renowned for creating TV theme songs for iconic series such as Law & Order, The A-Team, and Hill Street Blues.

text: The Moscow Kremlin is a fortified complex located at the heart of Moscow, situated to the south of the Moskva River and to the east of Saint Basil's Cathedral and Red Square. This citadel is the best known example of a Russian kremlin and contains five palaces, four cathedrals, and the enclosing Kremlin Wall with its towers. Among these structures is the Grand Kremlin Palace, which served as the tsar's Moscow residence.
title: Moscow Kremlin

text: In the spring of 1984, an arm of the United States Navy asked some of its civilian researchers to assess statistical process control and the work of several prominent quality consultants and to make recommendations as to how to apply their approaches to improve the Navy's operational effectiveness. The recommendation was to adopt the teachings of W. Edwards Deming, who is the correct answer to the question of who developed the concept of total quality management. text: The 2015 World Series marked the 111th edition of the championship series, serving as a best-of-seven playoff between the National League champion New York Mets and the American League champion Kansas City Royals. text: Realizing that gambling would be profitable for local business, the Nevada state legislature legalized gambling at the local level in 1931. This year also saw the county issue the first gambling license to the Northern Club, marking the beginning of Las Vegas's rise as the gaming capital of the world. Soon after, other casinos were licensed on Fremont Street, such as the Las Vegas Club and the Apache Hotel. Fremont Street subsequently became the first paved street in Las Vegas and received the city's first traffic light in 1931.
title: History of Las Vegas

text: Beijing, formerly romanized as Peking, is the capital of the People's Republic of China and the world's second most populous city proper. The city, located in northern China, is governed as a direct-controlled municipality under the national government with 16 urban, suburban, and rural districts. Beijing Municipality is surrounded by Hebei Province with the exception of neighboring Tianjin Municipality to the southeast; together the three divisions form the Jingjinji metropolitan region and the national capital region of China.
title: Beijing

text: Beijing is situated at the northern tip of the roughly triangular North China Plain, which opens to the south and east of the city. Mountains to the north, northwest, and western regions shield the city, protecting northern China's agricultural heartland from encroaching desert steppes. In the northwestern part of the municipality, specifically the areas of Yanqing County and Huairou District, the Jundu Mountains dominate the landscape, while the western section is framed by Xishan or the Western Hills. The Great Wall of China was constructed along the rugged topography of the northern section to defend against nomadic incursions from the steppes. Mount Dongling, located in the Western Hills and bordering Hebei Province, stands as the municipality's highest point with an altitude of 2,303 metres (7,556Â ft).
title: Beijing

text: Triple threat is the basketball position where a player facing a defender receives a pass but has not yet dribbled. The offensive player's feet are slightly wider than shoulder width and placed on the balls of their feet, with knees flexed and both hands on the ball in front of them or resting on their thigh. This stance presents the defender with an opponent able to move in any direction, as one foot acts as the pivot while the other is slightly ahead. From this position, the player can choose to jump-shoot, dribble (drive) past the defender, or pass it to a teammate. Additionally, the player can attempt to get the defender out of their defensive stance using jab steps and pump fakes.
title: Basketball moves

text: Named after French Minister of War André Maginot, the Maginot Line was a defensive system of concrete fortifications and obstacles constructed in the 1930s by France. Built along its borders with Italy, Switzerland, Germany, and Luxembourg, this line served to deter German invasion by forcing attackers to maneuver around the defenses. Due to French strategic planning, the fortifications did not reach the English Channel because the nation intended to launch an offensive into Belgium to counter a German attack.
title: Maginot Line

text: Ain't Living Long Like This is the debut studio album by American country music singer-songwriter Rodney Crowell, released in 1978 by Warner Bros. Records. Despite failing to enter the Top Country Albums chart and having several singles that did not reach the top 40, the album is widely regarded as one of Crowell's best and most influential works. Brett Hartenbach of Allmusic praises its songwriting and vocal delivery, noting that it showcases Crowell's talents as well as his ability to interpret the work of other writers. Most of the songs on this album were subsequently covered by various artists, including The Oak Ridge Boys and Alan Jackson. Although the cover art was redesigned in a 2002 re-release to improve legibility, the album's legacy remains strong.
title: Ain't Living Long Like This

text: The visible portion of the human face that houses the nostrils is the protruding nose, whose overall shape is primarily defined by the ethmoid bone and the nasal septum. This cartilaginous structure, which lies between the nostrils, distinguishes the nose's form. On average, the male nose is larger than that of a female.
title: Anatomy of the human nose

text: The septum is a composite (osseo-cartilaginous) structure located in the midline of the nose that divides it into two similar halves. This anatomical feature, along with the lateral nasal wall, paranasal sinuses, superior concha, middle concha, and inferior concha, forms the corresponding passages known as the superior meatus, middle meatus, and inferior meatus on the lateral nasal wall. The superior meatus serves as the drainage area for the posterior ethmoid bone cells and the sphenoid sinus, while the middle meatus provides drainage for the anterior ethmoid sinuses and for the maxillary and frontal sinuses. The inferior meatus provides drainage for the nasolacrimal duct.
title: Anatomy of the human nose

title: Wipro

text: ATP hydrolysis is the reaction by which chemical energy stored in the high-energy phosphoanhydride bonds of adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is released to produce work, such as mechanical energy in muscles. When one phosphate group is removed, the resulting product is adenosine diphosphate (ADP) and an inorganic phosphate (Pi). ADP can be further hydrolyzed to yield adenosine monophosphate (AMP) and another orthophosphate (Pi).
title: ATP hydrolysis

text: The first common style of shark tooth appeared in the Devonian period approximately four hundred million years ago. These needle-like teeth are found in the plentiful cladodont teeth of the devonian, four hundred million years ago. Sharks with needle-like teeth commonly feed on small to medium-sized fish, sometimes including small sharks. These teeth are especially effective for such prey because they can easily grip their slippery and narrow bodies. Modern examples include the blue shark and bull sharks. These sharks specifically use their teeth to feed on small prey like squid, flounder, stingrays, and even hammerhead sharks.
title: Shark tooth

text: Staci Keanan, whose real name was Anastasia Love Sagorsky, is an American actress best known for her roles in the television series My Two Dads (1987–1990) and Step by Step (1991–1998). She has also been credited as Stacy Keenan and Staci Love.
title: Staci Keanan

text: Neptune is the eighth and farthest known planet from the Sun in the Solar System. In the Solar System, it is the fourth-largest planet by diameter, the third-most-massive planet, and the densest giant planet. Neptune is 17 times the mass of Earth and is slightly more massive than its near-twin Uranus, which is 15 times the mass of Earth and slightly larger than Neptune.
title: Neptune

text: Like Jupiter and Saturn, Neptune's atmosphere is composed primarily of hydrogen and helium, along with traces of hydrocarbons and possibly nitrogen, but it contains a higher proportion of "ices" such as water, ammonia, and methane. However, its interior, like that of Uranus, is primarily composed of ices and rock,[12] which is why Uranus and Neptune are normally considered "ice giants" to emphasise this distinction.[13]
title: Neptune

text: The Gulf of Mexico basin is roughly oval and is approximately 810 nautical miles wide and floored by sedimentary rocks and recent sediments. It is connected to part of the Atlantic Ocean through the Florida Straits between the U.S. and Cuba, and with the Caribbean via the Yucatán Channel between Mexico and Cuba. With the narrow connection to the Atlantic, the Gulf experiences very small tidal ranges. The size of the Gulf basin is approximately 1.6 million km2. Almost half of the basin is shallow continental shelf waters. The basin contains a volume of roughly 2,500 quadrillion liters, which is equivalent to 550 quadrillion Imperial gallons, 660 quadrillion US gallons, or 2.5 million km3.
title: Gulf of Mexico

text: Vasoepididymostomy is a surgical procedure that involves connecting the epididymis to the vas deferens. This operation is particularly challenging because it requires anastomosing a single epididymal tubule with a diameter of .15-.25 mm to the vas deferens lumen, which has a diameter of .3-.4 mm. The procedure is indicated for patients suffering from congenital or acquired epididymal obstruction, as well as those who have failed previous attempts at vas deferens reconstruction. The technique attaches the vas deferens directly to the epididymis, the coiled tube located on the back of each testicle where sperm matures. While a vasectomy can cause blockages or breaks in either the vas deferens or the epididymis, this surgery is specifically utilized when sperm flow is blocked and a standard vasovasostomy is not effective. The connection is made above the point of blockage, ensuring that the sperm can travel from the epididymis to the vas deferens.
title: Vasoepididymostomy

text: The Iroquois was originally designated HU-1, which gave rise to the nickname Huey. This designation has persisted in common usage even after the official redesignation to UH-1 in 1962. The UH-1 first saw combat operations during the Vietnam War, with approximately 7,000 helicopters deployed. The Bell 204 and 205 are Iroquois versions developed specifically for the civil market.
title: Bell UH-1 Iroquois

text: Kirsten Simone Vangsness (born July 7, 1972) is an American actress and writer who currently stars as FBI Technical Analyst Penelope Garcia on the CBS drama series Criminal Minds.
title: Kirsten Vangsness

text: The fourth season of the Fox musical comedy-drama television series Glee premiered on September 13, 2012.
title: Glee (season 4)

text: Kozunak, the traditional sweet leavened bread prepared for Easter in Romania, is also known as Cozonac. This festive holiday food, which translates to "doll-shaped sweet bread," is a type of Stollen and is typically baked for Easter in Bulgaria, though it is also enjoyed during major holidays like Christmas and New Year's Day in Romania and Moldova.
title: Cozonac

text: The genus of the bald eagle is Haliaeetus, a name derived from the scientific term for "sea eagle" and the Latinized Greek word for "white head." This classification reflects the bird's distinctive appearance, specifically its white head and tail feathers which contrast with its darker body.
title: Bald eagle

text: Directed by the acclaimed filmmaker William Wyler, the 1946 American drama film *The Best Years of Our Lives* (also known as *Glory for Me and Home Again*) tells the story of three United States servicemen as they readjust to civilian life following their return from World War II. The production was conceived by Samuel Goldwyn, who was inspired to create a film about veterans after reading an August 7, 1944, article in Time regarding the challenges faced by men reentering society. While Goldwyn hired former war correspondent MacKinlay Kantor to write the screenplay, his initial work was first published as a novella titled *Glory for Me*, in which Kantor composed blank verse. Robert E. Sherwood subsequently adapted this novella into the final screenplay for the movie.
title: The Best Years of Our Lives

text: Coton in the Elms is a village and parish located in the English county of Derbyshire, situated at a distance of 70 miles from the coast. This makes it the furthest place in the United Kingdom from coastal waters.
title: Coton in the Elms

text: The ICD-10 code structure is defined by seven distinct characters, which encompass the disease category, its root cause, the specific body part involved, the level of severity, a placeholder for future extensions, and other details.
title: ICD-10

text: The pia mater, often described as a delicate membrane known as the "tender mother," is the specific meningeal layer that adheres tightly to the surface of the brain and spinal cord. This thin, fibrous tissue conforms to the brain's gyri and sulci, serving as a crucial interface where blood vessels pierce the membrane to nourish the central nervous system.
title: Meninges

text: Eddie Van Halen, lead guitarist of the hard rock band Van Halen, was asked to add a guitar solo to the song "Beat It" for the movie *Beat It*. When initially contacted by Jones, Van Halen thought he was receiving a prank call, but after establishing that the call was genuine, he borrowed an amplifier from guitarist Allan Holdsworth and recorded his guitar solo free of charge. Van Halen later stated, "I did it as a favor," and described himself as a complete fool, noting that he knew exactly what he was doing and only performed when he wanted to do it.
title: Beat It

text: In the final, hosts and pre-tournament favourites Uruguay defeated Argentina 4–2, becoming the first nation to win the World Cup.
title: 1930 FIFA World Cup

text: Named after Danish physicist Niels Bohr, the synthetic element known as Bohrium is represented by the symbol Bh and possesses an atomic number of 107. This radioactive substance is not found in nature but can be synthesized in a laboratory. While its most stable isotope, 270Bh, has a half-life of approximately 61 seconds, the unconfirmed isotope 278Bh may exhibit a longer half-life of about 690 seconds.
title: Bohrium

text: The IUPAC adopted the name bohrium for element 107 in 1997, following a recommendation by a committee to avoid confusion with boron and its oxyanions, bohrate and borate. This naming decision was made despite the discoverers' concerns about potential misinterpretation, as the matter was resolved through the Danish branch of IUPAC, which voted in favor of the name. Consequently, the designation bohrium for element 107 was recognized internationally, and the names of the respective oxyanions of boron and bohrium remain unchanged despite their homophony.
title: Bohrium

text: In the episode titled "Kobol's Last Gleaming," Commander Adama dispatches Boomer to eliminate a basestar orbiting Kobol, where she discovers multiple Number Eight clones identical to herself. Determined not to accept her identity as a Cylon, she personally detonates the device. Upon returning to Galactica, her hidden programming activates and she shoots Commander Adama twice in the chest, leaving him in a coma. She is subsequently placed in the brig and subjected to violent interrogation by Colonel Tigh, who assumes command during Adama's incapacitation. Tyrol is also suspected of being a Cylon due to his connection with her, leading to his imprisonment alongside her. He forbids her from speaking to him or touching him, asserting that she is a machine and nothing resembling him.
title: Number Eight (Battlestar Galactica)

text: The 1927 adventure novel *The Treasure of the Sierra Madre*, originally titled *Der Schatz der Sierra Madre*, was written by the bilingual German author B. Traven, whose identity remains unknown. In the book, two destitute American men in the 1920s join an older American man in Mexico to prospect for gold. John Huston adapted the book as a 1948 film of the same name.
title: The Treasure of the Sierra Madre

text: In the opening scene of the film Star Wars, the massive Imperial vessel known as the Devastator serves as Darth Vader's flagship, which is seen pursuing the smaller Tantive IV across the desert landscape of Tatooine.
title: Star Destroyer

text: Nala is the daughter of Sarafina, the best friend and later wife of Simba, Kiara, and Kion's mother. While she is a prominent character in The Lion King, she makes minor appearances in Simba's Pride, The Lion King 1½, and The Lion Guard.
title: List of The Lion King characters

text: List of Star Wars: The Clone Wars episodes: On March 11, 2013, Lucasfilm announced that Star Wars: The Clone Wars would be "winding down," effectively canceling the series as Lucasfilm ended its contract with Cartoon Network, following its acquisition by Disney. The unreleased episodes that had already been produced are referred to as "bonus content." On January 16, 2014, the German television network Super RTL announced their plans to air the "bonus content" as a sixth season, which would consist of 13 episodes. Season 6, along with the other seasons and the feature film, were made available on Netflix on March 7, 2014.
title: List of Star Wars: The Clone Wars episodes

text: Chilliwack is a Canadian rock band centered on the singer and guitarist Bill Henderson, which started off with a more Progressive rock sound that incorporated elements of folk, jazz, and blues, before moving towards a more straight-ahead hard rock/pop rock sound by the mid-70s. They were active from 1970 to 1988, while Henderson reformed the band in 1997. Their six best-selling songs were "My Girl (Gone, Gone, Gone)", "I Believe", "Whatcha Gonna Do", "Fly At Night", "Crazy Talk", and "Lonesome Mary".
title: Chilliwack (band)

text: The financing activities section of the cash flow statement details the inflow of cash from investors like banks and shareholders, alongside the outflow of cash to shareholders in the form of dividends. This section also encompasses other activities affecting the company's long-term liabilities and equity.
title: Cash flow statement

text: The 180th meridian, also known as the antimeridian, represents the 180th degree of longitude situated either 180 degrees east or west of the Prime Meridian. This significant line forms a great circle that divides the Earth into two hemispheres and is frequently utilized as the reference for the International Date Line, which largely follows the path through the Pacific Ocean. However, it is important to note that this meridian does not stay entirely within the open waters; it passes through regions in Russia, Fiji, and Antarctica.
title: 180th meridian

text: Dirk Benedict, born Dirk Niewoehner on March 1, 1945, is an American actor and author best known for his role as Lieutenant Templeton "Faceman" Peck in The A-Team television series.
title: Dirk Benedict

text: Eyjafjallajökull, a location in Iceland, experienced volcanic activity in 2010 that, despite being relatively modest in scale, triggered significant air travel disruptions across western and northern Europe. While the initial impact lasted for six days in April, additional local disturbances persisted into May. The official cessation of the eruption occurred in October 2010, a timing determined by the failure of snow to melt on the glacier. Between April 14 and 20, ash from this event blanketed extensive areas of Northern Europe, leading approximately 20 nations to close their commercial airspace and impacting roughly 10 million travelers.
title: 2010 eruptions of Eyjafjallajökull

text: In the United States, the poverty threshold is an annual income figure updated by the Census Bureau for statistical purposes. For example, in 2015, the poverty threshold for a single person under 65 was an annual income of US$11,770, while the threshold for a family group of four, including two children, was US$24,250. According to U.S. Census Bureau data released on 13 September 2011, the nation's poverty rate rose to 15.1 percent in 2010.
title: Poverty threshold

text: The Steelers were the first team since the 2011 Green Bay Packers to play on both Thanksgiving and Christmas Day. The team also improved upon their 10–6 record from 2015. Le'Veon Bell made his career first playoff appearance with the Steelers in the 2016–17 playoffs. The Steelers went on to defeat the Miami Dolphins in the Wild Card round and the Kansas City Chiefs in the Divisional round before losing to the eventual Super Bowl champion New England Patriots 36–17 in the AFC Championship Game. This was the Steelers' first appearance in the AFC Championship Game since the 2010–11 NFL Season.
title: 2016 Pittsburgh Steelers season

text: A flag designed by John McConnell in 1969 for the first Earth Day features a dark blue field charged with "The Blue Marble," a renowned NASA photograph of Earth as viewed from outer space. This inaugural edition of McConnell's flag relied on screen-printing and utilized distinct coloration, with oceans and land rendered in blue while clouds appeared white. McConnell presented his flag to the United Nations as a symbol worthy of consideration.
title: Flag of Earth

text: Distance is a scalar quantity representing the magnitude of a straight line between two locations, whereas displacement is a vector quantity that includes both magnitude and direction.
title: Distance

text: The distance covered by a vehicle, person, animal, or object along a curved path from a point A to a point B should be distinguished from the straight-line distance from A to B. For example, whatever the distance covered during a round trip from A to B and back to A, the displacement is zero as start and end points coincide. In general the straight-line distance does not equal distance travelled, except for journeys in a straight line.
title: Distance

text: James Martin Lafferty (born July 25, 1985) is an American actor, director and producer who achieved fame for his role as Nathan Scott on The CW teen drama One Tree Hill, a series he appeared in from 2003 to 2012.
title: James Lafferty

text: This annual college football bowl game, officially known as the Citrus Bowl presented by Overton's, Camping World stadium, and marine supply, is hosted in Orlando, Florida. It is currently operated by Florida Citrus Sports, the same non-profit group that manages the Camping World Bowl and Florida Classic.
title: Citrus Bowl

title: Over the Garden Wall

text: Elizabeth Dean Lail, born in 1992, is an American actress who gained fame for portraying the character Anna in the ABC series Once Upon a Time.
title: Elizabeth Lail

text: The phonograph was invented in 1877 by Thomas Edison. While other inventors had produced devices that could record sounds, Edison's phonograph was the first to be able to reproduce the recorded sound. His phonograph originally recorded sound onto a tinfoil sheet wrapped around a rotating cylinder. A stylus responding to sound vibrations produced an up and down or hill-and-dale groove in the foil.
title: Phonograph

text: Thomas Alva Edison conceived the principle of recording and reproducing sound between May and July 1877 as a byproduct of his efforts to "play back" recorded telegraph messages and to automate speech sounds for transmission by telephone. He announced his invention of the first phonograph, a device for recording and replaying sound, on November 21, 1877, and demonstrated the device for the first time on November 29. In December 1877, a young man came into the office of the Scientific American and placed before the editors a small, simple machine about which very few preliminary remarks were offered. The visitor without any ceremony whatever turned the crank, and to the astonishment of all present the machine said: "Good morning. How do you do? How do you like the phonograph?" The machine thus spoke for itself, and made known the fact that it was the phonograph.
title: Phonograph

text: American Idol, an American singing competition series created by Simon Fuller and produced by FremantleMedia North America, originally aired on Fox from June 11, 2002, until April 7, 2016. This event concluded the show after fifteen seasons, and the program officially ended on April 7, 2016.
title: American Idol

text: Tyrion Lannister, a dwarf of House Lannister, is the younger brother of Cersei and Jaime Lannister. Nicknamed "The Imp" or "Halfman," he was born when his mother died, an event Tywin Lannister blames on him. While not physically powerful, Tyrion possesses a cunning mind that often helps others underestimate him. In Season Three, he becomes the Master of Coin, a role he finds unprepared for. His marriage to Sansa Stark ends in tragedy: on the wedding night, he refuses to consummate the marriage and leaves her to sleep alone. This incident, combined with the death of his brother Robb, causes a rift between Tyrion and his father, Tywin, who accuses him of losing his mind. Tywin also claims he wanted to drown Tyrion at birth but stayed to fulfill his duty. During Season Four, Tyrion welcomes Prince Oberyn Martell to King's Landing for Joffrey's wedding. When Joffrey is poisoned, Tyrion is framed and arrested. He later claims Cersei knows his innocence but wants him dead. At his trial, Tyrion demands a trial by combat. He is challenged by Oberyn, who volunteers to fight Ser Gregor Clegane. When Oberyn is killed, Tyrion is sentenced to death, but Jaime frees him and arranges his escape. Tyrion confronts Tywin, only to find Shae, who testified against him. Tyrion strangles Shae and shoots Tywin with Joffrey's crossbow. He is then smuggled to Essos with help from Varys, where Tyrion convinces Varys to take him to Meereen to aid Daenerys Targaryen. Bound by Jorah Mormont, they travel to Meereen, where Tyrion explains his complex relationship with Daenerys. He warns her that winning the love of the common people and nobles will be difficult. Later, he joins her at the opening of Daznak's Pit to help defeat the Sons of the Harpy. During the battle, Tyrion survives by fleeing to the arena, where Drogon rescues him while Daenerys is spirited away on his back. In Season Six, Tyrion struggles to maintain peace in Meereen after the Sons of the Harpy burn the navy. Following an alliance with Theon and Yara Greyjoy, he advises Daenerys to break off her relationship with Daario. In gratitude for his loyalty, Daenerys names him her official Hand. In Season Seven, Tyrion's advice often conflicts with Daenerys's views, yet he successfully meets with Jamie to arrange a meeting between her and Cersei outside the city. At the Dragonpit meeting, a captured wight is produced to convince Cersei that the greatest threat is from beyond the Wall. When she refuses to listen, Tyrion risks his life to meet with his sister one last time, hoping to persuade her to help against the Wight Walkers.
title: List of Game of Thrones characters

text: James "Jamie" Dornan (born 1 May 1982) is an Irish actor, model, and musician who played the character Christian Grey in the Fifty Shades franchise from 2015 to the present.
title: Jamie Dornan

text: Liam Cunningham (born 2 June 1961) is an Irish stage and screen actor who is well known for his role as Davos Seaworth in the HBO epic-fantasy series Game of Thrones.
title: Liam Cunningham

text: On Opening Day, April 9, 1965, a sold-out crowd of 47,879 gathered for an exhibition game between the Houston Astros and the New York Yankees, where President Lyndon B. Johnson and his wife Lady Bird were in attendance alongside Texas Governor John Connally and Houston Mayor Louie Welch. Governor Connally tossed out the first ball for the first indoor game ever played, while Dick "Turk" Farrell of the Astros delivered the first pitch. Mickey Mantle, who played for the Houston Astros, was the first player to hit both a single and a home run in the Astrodome. The Astros subsequently defeated the Yankees, 2-1.
title: Astrodome

text: In Time is a 2011 American dystopian science fiction action thriller film written, directed, and produced by Andrew Niccol, starring Justin Timberlake, Amanda Seyfried, and Cillian Murphy. The movie depicts a society where people stop aging at age 25, while a new economic system treats time as currency and places a countdown clock on each person's arm. Originally released on October 28, 2011, the film centers on this unique time-based economy.
title: In Time

text: The decisive factor in the fall of 1862 and increasingly thereafter was the Battle of Antietam, where Lee's invasion was a failure and he barely escaped back to Virginia. It was now clear that no final, conclusive Confederate triumph could be anticipated, as the swift recession of the high Confederate tide was as visible in Britain as in America. Consequently, Palmerston and Russell dropped any notion of bringing a mediation-recognition program before the cabinet.
title: United Kingdom and the American Civil War

text: During the early years of the American Civil War, British officials including Prime Minister Lord Palmerston and Foreign Secretary Lord Russell weighed the strategic costs of recognizing the Confederacy, which threatened the merchant marine and national interests. Although a mediation effort was underway following the Second Battle of Manassas, the Union's decisive victory at the Battle of Antietam and President Lincoln's Emancipation Proclamation significantly altered British policy. These events, coupled with internal political pressures, compelled the government to reconsider and ultimately withdraw its support for the southern cause.
title: United Kingdom and the American Civil War

text: The Electoral College is the system by which the United States elects its president; each state receives a number of electors equal to its total of senators and representatives, plus three electors for the District of Columbia. There are a total of 538 electors, corresponding to the 435 representatives and 100 senators, plus the three electors for the District of Columbia as provided by the Twenty-third Amendment. The Constitution bars any federal official, elected or appointed, from being an elector. Since the mid-19th century when all electors have been popularly chosen, the Electoral College has elected the candidate who received the most popular votes nationwide, except in four elections: 1876, 1888, 2000, and 2016. In 1824, there were six states in which electors were legislatively appointed, rather than popularly elected, so the true national popular vote is uncertain; the electors failed to select a winning candidate, so the matter was decided by the House of Representatives.
title: Electoral College (United States)

text: Born on July 11, 1985, Robert Gillespie Adamson IV is an American actor who has portrayed the roles of Phil Sanders on Hollywood Heights and Charles Antoni on Lincoln Heights, and currently stars as Noah Newman on The Young and the Restless.
title: Robert Adamson (actor)

text: The botswana pula was introduced in 1976, replacing the South African rand at par, even after a 12% devaluation in May 2005.
title: Botswana pula

text: In the 1992 film Basic Instinct, Catherine Tramell serves as the primary antagonist, a serial killer who is also the love interest of the detective Nick Curran. The sequel, Basic Instinct 2, expands this narrative by pairing her with the troubled British psychologist Michael Glass.
title: Catherine Tramell

text: The Easter Bunny, also known as the Easter Rabbit or Easter Hare, is a folkloric figure symbolizing Easter, often depicted as a rabbit delivering eggs. Originating among German Lutherans, this creature originally served as a judge, assessing the behavior of children before the start of the Easter season. In legend, the figure carries colored eggs, candy, and toys to children's homes, creating a similarity to Santa Claus or the Christkind who bring gifts on the night before their respective holidays. This custom was first mentioned in Georg Franck von Franckenau's work, *De ovis paschalibus* ('About Easter Eggs'), in 1682, referring to a German tradition where an Easter Hare brought eggs for children.
title: Easter Bunny

text: Star Trek: Discovery premiered on September 19, 2017, at ArcLight Hollywood before debuting on CBS and CBS All Access on September 24. The rest of the 15-episode first season was streamed weekly on All Access, a release that led to record subscriptions for the service and positive reviews from critics who highlighted Martin-Green's performance. A second season was ordered in October 2017.
title: Star Trek: Discovery

text: The Pamplona encierro is the most popular event of the San Fermin festival, which is held every year from 6–14 July. The first bull running takes place on 7 July, followed by one on each of the following mornings of the festival, beginning every day at 8 am.
title: Running of the Bulls

text: In the first series of the UK game show *Take Me Out*, the successful couples conducted their date at FERNANDO'S! in Manchester, which is actually Club Bijou on Chapel Street. For the second series, the date took place abroad on the Isle of FERNANDO'S!, a fictional location based in Puerto de la Cruz, Tenerife. Previously the date took place in Cyprus. Successful couples leave the programme upstairs on the opposite side of the studio to the 'Love Lift', and a song, usually from the latin pop genre, will be played.
title: Take Me Out (UK game show)

text: Shirley Mae Jones (born March 31, 1934) is an American actress and singer who starred as the mother of five children in the musical situation-comedy television series The Partridge Family (1970–74), a role she played alongside her real-life stepson David Cassidy, son of Jack Cassidy.
title: Shirley Jones

text: The film Ek Anek Aur Ekta was directed by Vijaya Mulay.
title: Ek Anek Aur Ekta

text: While federal law treats airsoft guns as non-firearms and allows purchase by anyone, state and local regulations often impose age restrictions, such as California requiring buyers to be at least 18. Although the federal government does not mandate an age limit for sales, specific jurisdictions like California have ordinances that define airsoft as a spring-powered firearm, thereby restricting access to those over the age of 18.
title: Legal issues in airsoft

text: While jelly beans were first mentioned in Boston in 1861, they gained widespread recognition as Easter treats only by the 1930s. Specifically, during the 1930s, historians note that the candy's egg-like shape led to its association with Easter celebrations in the United States.
title: Jelly bean

text: Although the custom of decorating evergreen trees in homes had existed for many years, the practice of placing a full tree within the home was a novelty in Britain that did not arrive until around two centuries ago. This tradition was first brought to the country by Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz, who served as George III's German-born wife and introduced the custom at a children's party in 1800. Although the novelty initially remained with the royal family, Queen Victoria, who was a child at the time, was familiar with the idea and placed a tree in her room every Christmas. Her own journal entry from Christmas Eve 1832 reveals her delight at the gesture.
title: Christmas tree

text: The Q'eqchi' are the 2nd largest ethnic group among the Maya people in Guatemala, following the K'iche' as the largest.
title: Maya peoples

text: Human iron metabolism is unique because most dietary iron is absorbed in the duodenum, where enterocytes of the duodenal lining utilize special molecules to facilitate entry into the body. For absorption to occur, iron must first be in its ferrous Fe2+ form, a step that is catalyzed by a ferric reductase enzyme known as duodenal cytochrome B (Dcytb) on the brush border. This enzyme reduces ferric Fe3+ to Fe2+, allowing the protein divalent metal transporter 1 (DMT1) to subsequently transport the iron across the enterocyte's cell membrane into the cell.
title: Human iron metabolism

text: In June 1992, Starbucks marked a significant milestone by becoming a publicly traded entity on the stock market, a development that occurred shortly after its initial public offering. The company's market value was already substantial, standing at US$271 million, while its revenue had surged from US$1.3 million in 1987 to US$73.5 million. This financial growth was accompanied by a notable expansion of its physical presence, as the 12% stake sold in the IPO raised approximately US$25 million, enabling the store count to double over the subsequent two years.
title: Starbucks

text: In the summer of 2011, regulations were updated to permit the use of sew-on embroidered skill badges, such as the President's Hundred Tab, on the left sleeve pocket flap, which is governed by a 3-tab-only rule. A tab that is an integral part of a unit patch, for instance, does not count against this restriction. The U.S. Army Chaplain insignia stands as the sole authorized branch insignia for the ACU, positioned 1/8 inch above the right name tape. This insignia may appear either as a metal pin-on or as a black embroidered option featuring Velcro fasteners.
title: Army Combat Uniform

text: Plant hormones are signal molecules produced within the plant and occur in extremely low concentrations. These hormones regulate cellular processes in targeted cells locally and, when moved to other locations, affect other functional parts of the plant. They determine the formation of flowers, stems, leaves, the shedding of leaves, and the development and ripening of fruit. Unlike animals, plants lack glands that produce and secrete hormones; instead, each cell is capable of producing hormones. Plant hormones shape the plant, affecting seed growth, time of flowering, the sex of flowers, senescence of leaves, and fruits. They influence which tissues grow upward and which grow downward, leaf formation and stem growth, fruit development and ripening, plant longevity, and even plant death. Hormones are vital to plant growth, and, lacking them, plants would be mostly a mass of undifferentiated cells. So they are also known as growth factors or growth hormones. The term 'Phytohormone' was coined by Went and Thimann and used in the title of their book in 1937.[1]
title: Plant hormone

text: The Supreme Court of the Philippines, colloquially known as the Corte Suprema, serves as the nation's highest judicial body under the Constitution, which grants it administrative supervision over all lower courts and their personnel. This institution is led by a Chief Justice and is composed of fifteen (15) Justices, including the Chief Justice.
title: Supreme Court of the Philippines

text: The title 101 Dalmatians (1996 film) centers on American video game designer Roger Dearly, who lives with his pet dalmatian Pongo in London. One day, Pongo sets his eyes on a beautiful female dalmatian named Perdy. After a frantic chase through the streets of London that ends in St. James's Park, Roger discovers that Pongo likes Perdy. Her owner, Anita Campbell-Green (Joely Richardson) falls in love with Roger when they meet. They both fall into the lake as a result of their dogs chasing each other, but they return to Roger's home and Anita accepts his proposal. They get married along with Perdita and Pongo. Anita works as a fashion designer at the House of de Vil. Her boss, the pampered and very glamorous Cruella de Vil (Glenn Close), has a deep passion for fur, going so far as to have a taxidermist, Mr Skinner, skin a white tiger at the London Zoo to make it into a rug for her. Anita, inspired by her dalmatian, designs a coat made with spotted fur. Cruella is intrigued by the idea of making garments out of actual dalmatians, and finds it amusing that it would seem as if she was wearing Anita's dog.
title: 101 Dalmatians (1996 film)

text: Kit Harington portrays Jon Snow on the HBO series Game of Thrones. His storyline follows the character's plot arc from the novel series, though season 6 and season 7 of the TV adaptation continue on from the events of Martin's latest published installment. Harington was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Supporting Actor in a Drama Series for the role in 2016. He was also nominated for a Saturn Award for Best Supporting Actor on Television in 2012, 2016 and 2017.
title: Jon Snow (character)

text: Where's Wally?, originally titled Where's Wally and later retitled as Where's Waldo, is a British children's puzzle book series created by Martin Handford. The collection features detailed double-page illustrations showing numerous individuals performing various activities at specific locations, challenging readers to locate the character named Wally within the crowd.
title: Where's Wally?

text: The left anterior descending artery is a branch of the left coronary artery, also known as the anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery or anterior descending branch. Occlusion of this artery is often called the widow-maker infarction due to a high death risk.
title: Anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery

text: While Real Madrid holds the record for the most La Liga titles with a total of 33, the club's only Spanish team to have won the treble twice is Barcelona, who achieved this feat in 2015. The most recent club to win the league, aside from Real Madrid and Barcelona, is Atlético Madrid, who secured the title in the 2013–14 season.
title: List of Spanish football champions

text: Mall of America (commonly, locally known as "MOA" or "the mall") is a shopping mall located in Bloomington, Minnesota, United States (a suburb of the Twin Cities). Opened in 1992, it is the second largest mall in terms of leaseable space, the largest mall in the United States in terms of total floor area (including Nickelodeon Universe), and the twelfth largest in the world.
title: Mall of America

text: "I Wanna Be Sedated" is a track by the American punk rock group the Ramones, one of their most famous compositions. Originally appearing on their fourth album, Road to Ruin, in September 1978, the song served as the B-side to the UK single "She's the One," which hit the charts on September 21, 1978.
title: I Wanna Be Sedated

text: In modern times, the most frequent sinitic designation for China is Zhōngguó, derived from the characters zhōng (central) and guó (state). While the connotation of "nation" has emerged in contemporary usage, the term historically referred to the "Central States," signifying a culturally distinct core area centered on the Yellow River valley, as opposed to the tribal periphery. This specific meaning did not persist prior to the Qin unification. Consequently, during later periods, "Zhongguo" was not employed in this sense; instead, dynastic names were utilized for the state, such as "Han dynasty," "Tang dynasty," "The Great Ming," and "The Great Qing." Until the nineteenth century, when a common legal language was required by the international system, no fixed or unique name was necessary.
title: Names of China

text: The Cash Cab is equipped with ten cameras: one on the host, three on the passengers, one pointing forward from the back window of the cab, and three (front, left and right) in the advertising shell on the roof of the cab showing the passing streetscape. The rear of the cab behind the seats contains ten recording decks and other production equipment. The staff provide logistical information and questions by way of a walkie-talkie and earpiece worn by the host.

text: During the first half of 1349 the Black Death spread northwards, and by December 1349 conditions were returning to relative normalcy, marking the end of the plague in England.
title: Black Death in England

text: While the commercial introduction of the ouija board occurred on July 1, 1890, it was not immediately recognized as a parlor game. Instead, American spiritualist Pearl Curran popularized its use as a divining tool during World War I. Despite this shift, spiritualists in Ohio continued to employ a talking board very similar to a modern ouija board in 1886 to ostensibly enable faster communication with spirits.
title: Ouija

title: The Glass Castle (film)

text: While Brazil maintains its status as the world's largest coffee exporting nation, Vietnam recently achieved a significant milestone by tripling its exports between 1995 and 1999, emerging as a major producer of robusta seeds. Additionally, Indonesia holds the third-largest position among exporters, while organic coffee from Honduras is experiencing rapid growth due to its favorable climate and rich soil conditions.

It debuted on the Billboard Hot 100 on January 2, 1971 and hit the top of the chart on February 13, 1971, staying there for five weeks. It also reached number six on the R&B chart and Billboard ranked it as the No. 4 song for 1971. Both "One Bad Apple" and the Donny Osmond-credited single "Sweet and Innocent" are on the 1970 album Osmonds, which was certified Gold by the RIAA on February 4, 1971.

text: In American and Canadian professional football, the offensive team requires a minimum of seven players to be positioned on the line of scrimmage. Among these seven, only the two players at the ends of the line are designated as eligible receivers; however, the remaining four players in the backfield—including the quarterback—are also eligible. A quarterback adopting a T-formation stance behind center is not eligible unless he legally moves at least one yard behind the line of scrimmage or onto the end of the line, remains stationary for one second before the snap, and is not counted toward the seven men required on the line.
title: Eligible receiver

text: Super Bowl LII, the final game of the 2017 NFL season, took place on February 4, 2018, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota. In this match, the Philadelphia Eagles secured victory over the New England Patriots, 41–33, marking the first time the Eagles had won a Super Bowl and their first NFL championship since 1960. This event was notable as the second Super Bowl ever hosted in Minneapolis, the northernmost city to host the game, following Super Bowl XXVI in 1991, and it was also the sixth Super Bowl played in a cold-weather city.
title: Super Bowl LII

Regular one-hour episodes subsequently aired Thursdays from March 1 through May 10, with the first season continuing until new episodes began on May 31.

title: Common myna

text: The manga begins in 2001, when the protagonist Giorno Giovanna, who resembles the character Haruno Shiobana, arrives in Naples. This encounter sets the stage for the story, as Giorno attempts to steal Koichi Hirose's luggage to obtain a skin sample of the latter. However, his plan is thwarted when he is stopped by Koichi's Stand, Echoes Act Three. Recognizing his own Stand power as akin to Gold Experience, Giorno then strives to become a mafia boss in Naples to improve the city and address issues regarding drug availability among young people.
