title: Diastema

text: The CN Tower features a metal staircase that reaches the main deck level after 1,776 steps, and the SkyPod 100 meters (328 feet) above it after 2,579 steps; it is the tallest metal staircase on Earth. These stairs are intended for emergency use only and are not open to the public, except for two times per year for charity stair-climb events. The average climber takes approximately 30 minutes to climb to the base of the radome, but the fastest climb on record is 7 minutes and 52 seconds in 1989 by Brendan Keenoy, an Ontario Provincial Police officer. In 2002, Canadian Olympian and Paralympic champion Jeff Adams climbed the stairs of the tower in a specially designed wheelchair. The stairs were originally on one of the three sides of the tower (facing north), with a glass view, but these were later replaced with the third elevator pair and the stairs were moved to the inside of the core. Top climbs on the new, windowless stairwell used since around 2003 have generally been over ten minutes.
title: CN Tower

text: South Sudan was eventually approved for membership to the East African Community in March 2016, and signed a treaty of accession in April 2016. It had six months to ratify the agreement, which it did on 5 September, at which point it formally acceded to the community. It does not yet participate to the same extent as the other members.
title: East African Community

text:
Over (cricket)
Since the 1979/80 season, Test cricket has utilized six balls per over, a change that marked the end of a system where overs originally featured four balls. Prior to this transition, the number of balls varied globally, often matching the format of first-class matches in the specific country where the test match was being played.
title: Over (cricket)

text: The Speaker of the House is elected by the House of Representatives, which elects the Speaker on the first day of every new Congress. In the event of the death, resignation, or removal from the Chair of an incumbent Speaker, the House of Representatives also elects the Speaker. The Clerk of the House of Representatives requests nominations, normally two, one from each major party. The Clerk then calls the roll of the Representatives, each Representative indicating the surname of the candidate the Representative is supporting. Representatives are not restricted to voting for one of the nominated candidates and may vote for any person, even for someone who is not a member of the House at all. They may also abstain by voting "present".
title: Speaker of the United States House of Representatives

text: In the tenth season of My Three Sons, 1969-1970, Steve remarries by taking widowed teacher Barbara Harper, who is played by Beverly Garland, as his wife. This new spouse brings with her a five-year-old daughter named Dorothy "Dodie" (Dawn Lyn), whom Steve subsequently adopts. Although Dodie initially fears Steve's intentions, he explains that he wants her to always remember and love him, even though he is no longer alive. Consequently, Steve hopes she will come to love him as well.
title: My Three Sons

text: According to Chinese mythology, there are four major Dragon Kings who serve as guardians of the Four Seas. These deities represent distinct bodies of water, with the East Sea aligned to the East China Sea, the South Sea corresponding to the South China Sea, the West Sea often associated with the Qinghai Lake and beyond, and the North Sea sometimes linked to Lake Baikal.
title: Chinese dragon

text: Naz Khialvi (1947 â€" 12 December 2010) was a Pakistani lyricist and radio broadcaster, who is mainly known for his Sufi verse *Tum Ek Gorakh Dhanda Ho* (You are a Puzzle), later sung by Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, a legendary Qawwali singer, making both of them a household name. He also hosted a radio programme, Sandhal Dharti at Faisalabad radio station for 27 years.[1]
title: Naz Khialvi

text: The term John Hancock has become a synonym in the United States for one's signature, a fact that remains true because John Hancock served as president of the Second Continental Congress and was the first and third Governor of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts. He is remembered for his large and stylish signature on the United States Declaration of Independence, so much so that the term John Hancock has become a synonym in the United States for one's signature.
title: John Hancock

text: The United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development, commonly referred to as Rio 2012 or Rio+20, was hosted by Brazil in Rio de Janeiro between 13 and 22 June 2012. This event served as a 20-year follow-up to the 1992 Earth Summit, which took place in the same city, and marked the 10th anniversary of the 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development in Johannesburg.
title: United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development

text: Two years after his release from Camp Green Lake, Theodore "Armpit" Johnson is residing in Austin, Texas, where he attempts to establish a stable existence by excavating deep holes and providing care for his neighbor Ginny McDonald, a ten-year-old girl with cerebral palsy. During his employment at the mayor's residence, Armpit is approached by Rex "X-Ray" Washburn, a former friend from Camp Green Lake seeking financial assistance for a ticket scalping plan involving the upcoming performance of teen pop star Kaira Deleon.
title: Small Steps (novel)

text: Pretty Little Liars season 7 consisted of 20 episodes, with ten airing in the summer of 2016 and the remaining ten from April 2017. The season premiered on June 21, 2016, on Freeform, and production began at the end of March 2016. This was the final season of the series, which was confirmed on August 29, 2016.
title: Pretty Little Liars (season 7)

text: The term 'robot' originates from the Czech word *robota*, which translates to "forced labor." While the word was first used to describe a fictional humanoid in a 1920 play by Karel Čapek, it was actually his brother Josef Čapek who invented the term.
title: Robot

text: The term 'robot' was first applied as a term for artificial automata in a 1920 play R.U.R. by the Czech writer, Karel Čapek. However, Josef Čapek was named by his brother Karel as the true inventor of the term robot.[7][8] The word 'robot' itself was not new, having been in Slavic language as robota (forced laborer), a term which classified those peasants obligated to compulsory service under the feudal system widespread in 19th century Europe (see: Robot Patent).[41][42]
title: Robot

text: The Geographic South Pole is situated on the continent of Antarctica, a location that remains constant despite the shifting tectonic plates that have moved continents over time. This position places the pole atop a featureless, barren, windswept, and icy plateau, which stands at an altitude of 2,835 metres (9,301 ft) above sea level. While the land surface under the ice sheet is near sea level, the ice itself is estimated to be about 2,700 metres (9,000 ft) thick, and the pole is located approximately 1,300 km (800 mi) from the nearest open sea at the Bay of Whales.
title: South Pole

text: In 1947, a full-scale conflict erupted between the Viet Minh and France, a situation that France viewed as a precursor to the end of colonial rule globally. Consequently, France established a semi-independent State of Vietnam within its Union, with Bảo Đại serving as the Head of State. While the Viet Minh sought support from China as Mao Zedong consolidated power in China, the Chinese Communist Party pressured the Vietnamese Communist Party under First Secretary Trường Chinh to adopt a style of revolution similar to theirs. This led to a purge of "bourgeois and feudal" elements from the Viet Minh ranks, resulting in a ruthless and bloody land reform campaign and the denunciation of "bourgeois and feudal" tendencies in arts and literature. Many true patriots and devoted Communist revolutionaries in the Viet Minh suffered mistreatment or were even executed during these movements, while others became disenchanted and left the Viet Minh. The United States became strongly opposed to Hồ Chí Minh. In the 1950s, the government of Bảo Đại gained recognition by the United States and the United Kingdom.
title: History of Vietnam since 1945

text: Wal-Mart Stores, Inc., doing business as Walmart, is an American multinational retail corporation headquartered in Bentonville, Arkansas, founded by Sam Walton in 1962 and incorporated on October 31, 1969. As of October 31, 2017, the company operated 11,703 stores and clubs across 28 countries under various names, including Walmart in the United States and Canada, Walmart de México y Centroamérica in Mexico, Asda in the United Kingdom, and the Seiyu Group in Japan. The organization also maintains wholly owned operations in Argentina, Chile, Brazil, and Canada, while owning and operating Sam's Club retail warehouses.
title: Walmart

text: Roger Dean Stadium is one of only two stadiums in Florida to host two Major League Baseball teams annually for spring training: the Miami Marlins and St. Louis Cardinals. In both venues, the teams share the main stadium where the games are played.
title: Roger Dean Stadium

text: The term "social justice" was first used explicitly in the 1840s. A Jesuit priest named Luigi Taparelli is typically credited with coining the term, and it spread during the revolutions of 1848 with the work of Antonio Rosmini-Serbati. In the late industrial revolution, progressive American legal scholars began to use the term more, particularly Louis Brandeis and Roscoe Pound. From the early 20th century it was also embedded in international law and institutions; the preamble to establish the International Labour Organization recalled that "universal and lasting peace can be established only if it is based upon social justice." In the later 20th century, social justice was made central to the philosophy of the social contract, primarily by John Rawls in A Theory of Justice (1971). In 1993, the Vienna Declaration and Programme of Action treats social justice as a purpose of human rights education.
title: Social justice

text: The specific phrase "social justice" first emerged in the 1840s, a period when Catholic thinkers like the Jesuit Luigi Taparelli, drawing on St. Thomas Aquinas, offered the first modern definition of the concept. Taparelli critiqued competing theories of capitalism and socialism for their reliance on subjective Cartesian thinking, arguing that such approaches fractured the unity of society found in Thomistic metaphysics. Although John Stuart Mill later articulated a similar vision in 1861, the 1840s remains the earliest documented usage of the exact term in this context.
title: Social justice

text: The Star-Spangled Banner became law to require standing for the national anthem on June 22, 1942, when the legislation was revised to mandate that those in uniform salute while others simply stand at attention. This initial instruction, which also specified that men should remove their hats and women place their hands over their hearts, was later refined on December 23, 1942, to further clarify that hand placement and uniform saluting occurred only when the flag was displayed. Subsequent revisions in 1976 and 1998 simplified these rules, ultimately establishing the current standard where individuals in uniform salute regardless of flag visibility, while civilians stand at attention with hands over their hearts.
title: The Star-Spangled Banner

text: Dolley Madison popularized the First Ladyship by engaging in efforts to assist orphans and women, by dressing in elegant fashions and attracting newspaper coverage, and by risking her life to save iconic treasures during the War of 1812. Madison set the standard for the ladyship and her actions were the model for nearly every First Lady until Eleanor Roosevelt in the 1930s.
title: First Lady of the United States

text: Clarified butter, historically referred to as smen, has long served as the preferred medium for cooking in the Balkans and Middle East. While olive oil dominates in Mediterranean coastal regions, its consumption varies by religion; Christians abstain from it during Lent when meat and dairy are excluded, whereas Jews use it as a substitute for animal fats like butter to prevent the mixing of meat and dairy products.
title: Middle-Eastern cuisine

text: Phosphorus pentoxide is a chemical compound with molecular formula P4O10 (with its common name derived from its empirical formula, P2O5). This white crystalline solid is the anhydride of phosphoric acid and serves as a powerful desiccant and dehydrating agent.
title: Phosphorus pentoxide

text: The Cornett family currently manages Spirit of the Suwannee Music Park by overseeing various improvements designed to enhance entertainment, hiking, canoeing, camping, and other activities. The park provides diverse camping options that include primitive camping, RV camping, and furnished models, while also offering a tree house for special occasions.
title: Spirit of the Suwannee Music Park

text: The actor Sebastian Shaw was famous for his early work in Shakespeare plays and for his role as an unmasked and redeemed Anakin Skywalker in the original *Return of the Jedi*.
title: Sebastian Shaw (actor)

text: In the 1982 film Return of the Jedi, the final installment of the original Star Wars trilogy, the character of Anakin Skywalker appeared in a single scene aboard Death Star II. This moment served as the emotional climax of the movie, where the character Luke Skywalker unmasks his father as he dies. Although David Prowse performed the action sequences and James Earl Jones provided the voice, the casting crew hired Sebastian Shaw to portray the redeemed, unmasked, dying Anakin Skywalker, a role that is the answer to the question who is under the mask of Darth Vader.
title: Sebastian Shaw (actor)

text: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone is a fantasy novel written by British author J. K. Rowling. It is the first novel in the Harry Potter series and Rowling's debut novel, first published in 1997 by Bloomsbury.
title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone

text: James P. Flynn appeared in many films shot in the New England area, where he was cast as a judge in the Boston-based film Good Will Hunting in 1997. Later, he acted in the 1999 film The Cider House Rules and What's the Worst That Could Happen? in 2001. He was also a truck driver for movie production equipment during the filming of My Best Friend's Girl in 2008. Boston actor Tom Kemp remarked: "[The film The Departed] wouldn't be a Boston movie without me, a Wahlberg, and Jimmy Flynn from the teamsters."
title: Jimmy Flynn

text: In 1921, the Assam Provincial Congress Committee was formed with its headquarters at Guwahati, and Tarun Ram Phukan became its president.
title: Tarun Ram Phukan

text: Linda Davis is the singer of the song "Does He Love You," a collaboration between Reba McEntire and the songwriter Sandy Knox. This track was recorded as a duet by American country music artists Reba McEntire and Linda Davis and was released in August 1993 as the first single from Reba's album Greatest Hits Volume Two. It is one of country music's several songs about a love triangle.
title: Does He Love You

text: Accounts receivable represents a legally enforceable claim for payment held by a business for goods supplied and/or services rendered by customers or clients who have ordered but not yet paid. These amounts are typically presented in the form of invoices issued by the business and sent to the customer to facilitate payment within a specified time frame. Consequently, accounts receivable appears on a balance sheet as an asset; it constitutes one of the series of accounting transactions involved in billing a customer for goods and services they have requested. While these accounts differ from notes receivable, which arise from formal legal instruments known as promissory notes, the core definition of accounts receivable relies on the issuance of invoices for unpaid orders.
title: Accounts receivable

text: In the film *The Lost City of Z*, Manley passes away while serving in the trenches during the Battle of the Somme, a tragedy that leaves Fawcett temporarily blinded after a chlorine gas attack.
title: The Lost City of Z (film)

text: Hydrogen peroxide is a toxic byproduct generated in human and animal cells through various biochemical reactions. While the specific enzymes responsible for this process vary, the class of biological enzymes known as SOD (superoxide dismutase) is found in nearly all living cells. These enzymes facilitate the conversion of superoxide into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide, which are subsequently broken down into harmless water and oxygen by catalase.
title: Hydrogen peroxide

text: The Data Protection Act 1998, designated as c 29, is a United Kingdom Act of Parliament enacted to safeguard personal data housed within computers or organized paper filing systems. This legislation builds upon the EU Data Protection Directive 1995 by establishing the framework for data processing and movement. While the Act's provisions do not universally apply to domestic activities, such as maintaining a personal address book, anyone legally holding personal data for other purposes must comply with its requirements, subject to certain exemptions. To ensure lawful processing, the Act establishes eight core data protection principles.
title: Data Protection Act 1998

text: The London terminus for the Eurostar service is St Pancras International, a key British destination alongside other hubs in Kent such as Ebbsfleet and Ashford. While the route extends to various international cities like Calais, Lille, and Brussels, the primary London stop remains St Pancras International. Additionally, the network includes direct seasonal services to French cities including Lyon, Avignon, and Marseille, as well as to the French Alps during winter months.
title: Eurostar

text: Krypton-85 is a radioactive isotope with a half-life of 10.756 years and a maximum decay energy of 687 keV. It decays into stable, non-radioactive rubidium-85. Its most common decay mode, accounting for 99.57% of all decays, is by beta particle emission with a maximum energy of 687 keV and an average energy of 251 keV. The second most common decay pathway, occurring at a probability of 0.43%, also involves beta particle emission with a maximum energy of 173 keV, followed by gamma ray emission of 514 keV. Other decay modes have very small probabilities and emit less energetic gammas. There are 33 other known isotopes of krypton.
title: Krypton-85

text: The track "Every Light in the House," written by Kent Robbins, was recorded by American country music artist Trace Adkins. Released in August 1996 as the second single from his debut album *Dreamin' Out Loud*, this song marked Adkins' first Top 5 hit on the Hot Country Singles & Tracks chart, peaking at #3.
title: Every Light in the House

text: Based in Toronto, Lowe's established its first three Canadian locations on December 10, 2007, in Hamilton, Brampton, and Brantford. By February 1, 2008, the chain added three more stores to its portfolio, including new sites in Toronto, East Gwillimbury, and Brampton, alongside a location in Maple (Vaughan). While additional stores are currently under construction, the company has expanded its presence into Western Canada, opening three new sites in Calgary, Alberta, including one in late September 2010 and two in early 2011. There are now stores in British Columbia, Manitoba, and Saskatchewan. As of 2018, the company reported a total of 62 locations across the province. Each store represents an average investment of $20.5 million ($20.4 million USD).
title: Lowe's

title: Central processing unit

text: Anna Muttathupadathu, known by her religious name Saint Alphonsa, was a distinguished Indian religious sister and educator who passed away on July 28, 1946. She holds the distinction of being the first woman of Indian origin to be canonized as a saint by the Catholic Church, while also serving as the first canonised saint of the Syro-Malabar Catholic Church. Her feast day is observed annually on July 28th.
title: Saint Alphonsa

text: The harp serves as the symbol for the arms of Ireland. Historical records indicate that this designation appears in the oldest medieval rolls of arms, specifically the Wijnbergen Roll from c. 1280 in The Hague, which described a "D'azure a la harpe d'or" as belonging to the King of Ireland. While the harp is traditionally linked to King David, its presence on medieval Irish coinage by kings John and Edward I in the 12th and 13th centuries suggests it may have evolved from triangular designs used to distinguish Irish coins. The concept of the harp as Ireland's arms likely stems from a fictional character named le roi d'irelande in the legend cycle of Tristan or from a 13th-century bardic poem dedicated to a Gaelic King of Thomond.
title: Coat of arms of Ireland

text: Keeley Clare Julia Hawes (born 10 February 1976) is an English actress who played Detective Inspector Lindsay Denton in the second and third series of the BBC series Line of Duty (2014–2016).
title: Keeley Hawes

text: Tyler Perry has confirmed that in the 2018 film A Madea Family Funeral, Madea has another brother named Heathrow, who is also played by Perry and is described as a Vietnam war veteran.
title: Madea

text: Loyola University Chicago is named after St. Ignatius of Loyola, whose coat-of-arms features two wolves standing over a kettle, a design taken from the heraldic crest carved in the lintel on St. Ignatius' family home in Azpeitia, Spain. This imagery symbolizes the prosperity and generosity of the Loyola family, who, after feeding family, retainers, and soldiers, retained enough food to feed even the wild animals.
title: Loyola University Chicago

text: The eighth season of Shameless, an American comedy-drama television series, was announced on December 19, 2016, following the seventh season finale. While the show's production schedule began in 2016, the premiere date for the eighth season was set for November 5, 2017.
title: Shameless (season 8)

text: Rory Gilmore attends Yale University, her grandfather's alma mater, in season four of the show. Although her entire life she had wanted to go to Harvard, having decided that the benefits of Yale outweighed her dream of studying at Harvard. During her freshman year, Rory resides at Durfee Hall and shares a dorm room with Tana, Janet, and fellow Chilton alumna Paris Geller. She moves to Branford College, the same residential college that her grandfather, Richard Gilmore, lived in, at the beginning of her sophomore year. There she shares a dorm room with Paris. At Yale, Rory majors in English and pursues her interest in journalism; she wants to be a foreign correspondent and her role-model is Christiane Amanpour. She writes for the Yale Daily News and is its editor towards the end of her studies.
title: Rory Gilmore

text: The first Indianapolis 500 was held in 1911, where Ray Harroun was declared the first winner, driving the Marmon Wasp.
title: List of Indianapolis 500 winners

text: In the tale of the Ghost of Christmas Present, the spirit transports Scrooge through the city, revealing both the joy and the harsh realities of the season. As he wanders, he emits a little warmth from his torch while observing scenes of festivity and deprivation. Among the sights is a visit to Scrooge's nephew and the family of his impoverished clerk, Bob Cratchit. Scrooge shows particular concern for Cratchit's sick son, Tiny Tim, and inquires if the child will survive. The Ghost responds by warning that if these shadows remain unaltered, the child will die, and he further advises Scrooge to avoid his wicked tongue until he understands the true meaning of the surplus population. He concludes with a chilling remark that Scrooge might be less worthy of living than millions like the poor man's child.
title: Ghost of Christmas Present

text: The Lupus Foundation of America, a national voluntary health organization established in 1977, is headquartered in Washington, D.C. This group operates a network of chapters and support groups across the United States, aiming to resolve the mystery of lupus while providing care for its victims. The Foundation's primary mission is to enhance the quality of life for all individuals affected by lupus through research, education, and advocacy efforts.
title: Lupus Foundation of America

text: Aphasia is an inability to comprehend and formulate language because of damage to specific brain regions. This condition is characterized by significant impairment in one or several of the four communication modalities following acquired brain injury, including auditory comprehension, verbal expression, reading, writing, and functional communication.
title: Aphasia

text: Windows Media Player 11 supports the Windows Playlist (WPL) format, which serves as the native playlist file extension for audio content within the application.
title: Windows Media Player

text: Tom Stoppard's absurdist, existentialist tragicomedy, titled Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead, premiered in 1966 at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe. This work centers on two minor characters from Shakespeare's Hamlet, the courtiers Rosencrantz and Guildenstern, who serve as the primary protagonists. The narrative unfolds largely within the "wings" of Shakespeare's play, featuring brief appearances of major characters who enact fragments of the original scenes. Between these episodes, the two protagonists voice their confusion regarding the events of Hamlet that occur onstage without them, a state of confusion they possess due to having no direct knowledge of the plot.
title: Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead

text: In the film Madea Christmas, Connor's parents, Buddy (Larry the Cable Guy) and Kim (Kathy Najimy), arrive at Connor and Lacey's house to visit him for Christmas. They are told not to mention that Connor and Lacey are married because they do not know that Eileen has never wanted Lacey to marry a white man. Meanwhile, Eileen decides to get a Christmas tree and cuts down one with a yellow ribbon wrapped around it in the backyard, not knowing that Kim planted the tree in memory of her deceased father. When Eileen learns of this, she expresses no remorse, upsetting Kim. That night, Eileen walks in on Buddy and Kim, seeing Buddy with a sheet over his head, convincing her that Buddy is in the KKK. Now scared, she bars the door to the room that she and Madea are sharing.
title: A Madea Christmas (film)

text: The novel *The Fault in Our Stars*, written by John Green and published in January 2012, draws its title from a famous line by Shakespeare: "The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars, / But in ourselves, that we are underlings." The story follows Hazel Grace Lancaster, a 16-year-old girl battling cancer, who is compelled by her parents to join a support group. There, she meets Augustus Waters, a 17-year-old ex-basketball player and amputee, with whom she develops a romantic connection. A feature film adaptation starring Shailene Woodley and Ansel Elgort was released on June 6, 2014.
title: The Fault in Our Stars

text: On the morning of 10 June 1940, as the French government fled to Bordeaux during the German invasion and declared Paris an open city, Mussolini felt the conflict would soon end. He then declared war on Britain and France. As he said to the Army's Chief-of-Staff, Marshal Badoglio, the declaration of war on Britain and France marks the official start of Italy's involvement in the war.
title: Military history of Italy during World War II

title: Michael McDowell (racing driver)

text: Omar Khayyam (Persian pronunciation: [xæjˈjɑːm]; عمر خیّام) was a Persian mathematician, astronomer, and poet who lived from 1048 to 1131 CE.
title: Omar Khayyam

text: In J.P. Zenger High, Scott Hudson, a freshman, quickly discovers that the atmosphere is far more intimidating than middle school, where upperclassmen often steal lunch money and intimidate students. Scott finds himself in advanced classes like Honors English, which he loves despite the workload, and he is mentored by his teacher, Mr. Franka. Because he carries so many honors and college prep classes, he is not in the same classes as his best friends, Mitch, Patrick, and Kyle. Scott tries desperately to gain Julia Baskins's attention, a girl from his kindergarten class who has become very beautiful over the summer, but she quickly blends in with popular girls and attracts bullies. Scott also meets a classmate named Mouth, and he attempts to win her heart by joining the school paper, only to find she wrote only a single column. Scott runs for student council after she is also running, but she loses the election, causing him to resign. He also auditions for the school play and is selected as a crew member, but Julia is not cast or on the crew. Later, a new girl named Lee arrives with weird clothes and colored hair, and Scott realizes they share interests but he cannot overcome his crush on Julia. He also forms a friendship with a high school senior named Wesley, though they have little in common. The situation reaches a climax when Scott's mother announces she is pregnant. Scott copes by creating a tip book for his future sibling to help them survive high school, writing degrading terms for the baby like "Smelly" or "Blob of unformed goo," though he intends to be a good older brother. As time passes, Scott struggles to find his place and loses his best friends; Mitch gets a girlfriend and forgets the group, Patrick moves to Texas and then Japan, and Kyle joins the wrestling team and puts Scott down for having a crush on Julia. Eventually, Julia's boyfriend Vernon beats up Scott after Kyle reveals Scott has a crush on his girlfriend. Scott learns that actions can affect others after Mouth attempts suicide. He also discovers that his older brother, Bobby, struggles to find a job and barely reads. Finally, Scott's mother gives birth to a new baby boy named Sean, and while Julia eventually dates a nicer guy, she is close enough to Scott to give him a kiss on the cheek.
title: Sleeping Freshmen Never Lie

text: The song "How Do You Do It?" was penned by Mitch Murray, who initially offered it to Adam Faith and Brian Poole but declined both requests. Consequently, George Martin of EMI accepted the track for the new group he was producing, the Beatles, serving as the A-side for their debut album. Although the Beatles recorded the song in September 1962, they opposed its release, choosing to modify the demo-disc version provided by Murray. These alterations included a fresh introduction, vocal harmony, an instrumental interlude, minor lyric tweaks, and the removal of a specific half-step modulation in the final verse. Despite Murray's disapproval of these changes, the decision not to release the Beatles' version was driven primarily by business considerations, which ultimately led to "Love Me Do" becoming their first single. The official release of the song occurred in November 1995 on the Beatles retrospective Anthology 1 album.
title: How Do You Do It?

text: Seattle Slew (February 15, 1974 – May 7, 2002) was an American Thoroughbred race horse who won the Triple Crown in 1977—the tenth of twelve horses to accomplish the feat. He is the only horse to have won the Triple Crown while having been undefeated in any race previous.
title: Seattle Slew

text: The 2014 Rose Bowl was a college football bowl game played on January 1, 2014, at the Rose Bowl stadium in Pasadena, California. This 100th Rose Bowl Game featured the Michigan State Spartans against the Stanford Cardinal, who were the defending Rose Bowl champions and the Pac-12 Conference champions. The matchup was a rematch of the 1996 Sun Bowl.
title: 2014 Rose Bowl

text: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles first appeared in an American comic book published by Mirage Studios in 1984 in Dover, New Hampshire, marking the start of a series that has been reprinted by various publishers since that year. This initial publication was a single-issue work funded by a tax refund and a loan from Laird's uncle, designed to parody Marvel's Daredevil and New Mutants, Dave Sim's Cerebus, and Frank Miller's Ronin. The concept for the turtles originated from a humorous sketch by Eastman during a casual brainstorming session involving bad television, and the franchise continues to be a significant part of comic book history established in 1984.
title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles

text: In the season seven premiere, Morgan captures Doyle and Emily returns to the BAU to assist the team in finding who kidnapped Doyle's son. The team comes under fire from the judiciary panel for their retaliatory actions to avenge Prentiss's death, but everyone stands their ground to protect the team. Section Chief Erin Strauss later reveals to them that the committee was persuaded by Prentiss' defense and eventually decided to lift the BAU's suspensions although they will still be "keeping a close eye" on the members. Reid, who is still angry over her 'death' refuses to speak to her or JJ or even look them in the eye. At the end of "Proof", Prentiss talks it through with him and they make amends.
title: Emily Prentiss

text: Nebuchadnezzar, the Babylonian king, was the one who destroyed the First Temple and exiled the two tribes of Judah to Babylon. Following Zedekiah's rebellion and alliance with Pharaoh Hophra, Nebuchadnezzar returned to besiege Jerusalem, leading to the city's destruction in 587 BCE. The king demolished the city walls, the Temple, and the homes of the most important citizens. As punishment for his defiance, Zedekiah and his sons were captured, with the latter being executed before his father. Zedekiah was subsequently blinded and taken to Babylon, while the rest of the royal family and many others were also transported away. This event marked the end of the independent Kingdom of Judah, which was subsequently renamed Yehud as a Babylonian province. While rabbinic sources note discrepancies in the Jewish calendar regarding the specific year, they confirm that Nebuchadnezzar is the figure responsible for the destruction of the Temple and the exile of the tribes.
title: Babylonian captivity

text: Investment banker Harold Lee, who is persuaded to work while his colleagues leave for the weekend, and Kumar Patel, who attends a medical school interview but intentionally botches it to avoid acceptance, decide to get hamburgers after smoking marijuana and seeing an ad for the restaurant. After traveling to the nearest White Castle in New Brunswick, they discover it has been replaced by a "Burger Shack," yet they learn of another location in Cherry Hill.
title: Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle

text: The introduction of the Child Benefit Bill in the United Kingdom marked a significant policy shift by Barbara Castle in 1975, establishing a universal payment for each child that doubled the number of children covered. This new benefit was not means tested, distinguishing it from the family allowance it replaced, although such an attempt by the Callaghan government to introduce the scheme was thwarted in 1976 when cabinet papers were leaked to the Child Poverty Action Group.
title: Child benefits in the United Kingdom

text: Transition economies in Central and Eastern Europe and Central Asia experienced higher inequality of opportunity compared to some Western European developed economies, with the Balkans and Central Asia showing the most pronounced disparities. While legal regulations and access to education and health services often resulted in low inequality of opportunity related to gender in these regions, inequality related to labour practices, employment, entrepreneurship, and access to finance remained medium to high. Specifically, women in Central Asia faced significant barriers to accessing health services, a situation similar to that observed in Arab countries. Although many transition economies performed well with respect to primary and secondary education, they were notably weaker in training and tertiary education compared to other developed economies.
title: Transition economy

text: One More Light is the seventh studio album by American rock band Linkin Park, which was released on May 19, 2017, through Warner Bros. and Machine Shop. This record serves as the final Linkin Park album produced before the band's lead vocalist, Chester Bennington, passed away on July 20, 2017.
title: One More Light

text: Spain and the United Kingdom are currently involved in a territorial dispute concerning the island of Gibraltar. This British Overseas Territory, situated at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula, was captured in 1704 during the War of the Spanish Succession (1701–1714) and subsequently ceded to Britain in perpetuity by the Spanish Crown in 1713 via Article X of the Treaty of Utrecht. Although Spain attempted to reclaim the area through the thirteenth siege in 1727 and the Great siege between 1779 and 1783, British sovereignty was ultimately confirmed by later treaties signed in Seville (1729) and the Treaty of Paris (1783).
title: Disputed status of Gibraltar

text: The status of Gibraltar as a disputed territory stems from its historical reclamation by Spain, a policy that originated under General Franco and persists across successive governments following Spain's democratic transition. While the Gibraltarians firmly reject any claim to the island, no political party or pressure group in Gibraltar supports union with Spain. Furthermore, a 2002 referendum in which the people of Gibraltar rejected a joint sovereignty proposal between Spain and the United Kingdom demonstrated that both nations had reached a "broad agreement" on the issue. Consequently, the British Government has consistently stated that it would never enter into a sovereignty agreement without the explicit consent of the Gibraltar government and its people.
title: Disputed status of Gibraltar

text: Spain and the United Kingdom are in a dispute concerning the status of Gibraltar, an independent territory recognized by the United Nations. The UK granted the Gibraltar Constitution Order 2006, which designates the Governor of Gibraltar as the head of external affairs, defense, and internal security, while the local government handles other matters. Spain argues that this constitutional arrangement does not alter Gibraltar's position as a British colony, asserting that only the UK is empowered to discuss its affairs on the international scene.
title: Disputed status of Gibraltar

text: Thomas Mundy Peterson, born in 1824 and passing away in 1904, was the first African-American to register to vote in a United States election. He cast his ballot on March 31, 1870, under the provisions of the 15th Amendment to the Constitution.
title: Thomas Mundy Peterson

text: The East India Company was established on 31 December 1600, a date that was relatively late for the company to begin trading in the Indies. While the Portuguese Estado da India had previously dominated trade in the region for much of the 16th century, the first of half a dozen Dutch Companies sailed to the Indies in 1595. These vessels eventually amalgamated in March 1602 to form the United East Indies Company (VOC), which introduced the first permanent joint stock system in 1612, allowing investments in shares that could be traded on an exchange. Wealthy merchants and aristocrats owned the EIC's shares, whereas initially the government owned no shares and held only indirect control until permanent joint stock was established in 1657.
title: East India Company

text: On September 9, 2012, David Akers kicked a 63-yard field goal off the crossbar against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field, tying the NFL record for the longest field goal by kicking a 63-yard field goal off the crossbar against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. The record was originally set by Tom Dempsey and was shared with Jason Elam and Sebastian Janikowski until Broncos kicker Matt Prater broke the record with a 64-yard field goal on December 8, 2013.
title: David Akers

text: John Vincent Calipari, born February 10, 1959, is an American basketball coach who has served as the head coach of the University of Kentucky men's team since 2009. During his tenure, he led the team to an NCAA Championship victory in 2012, and he was previously named Naismith College Coach of the Year three times in 1996, 2008, and 2015. He was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2015.
title: John Calipari

text: The dermis or corium is a layer of skin located between the epidermis and subcutaneous tissues, primarily consisting of dense irregular connective tissue that cushions the body from stress and strain. This tissue is divided into two distinct areas: the superficial papillary region, which lies adjacent to the epidermis, and a deeper, thicker reticular dermis. Structural components of the dermis include collagen, elastic fibers, and an extrafibrillar matrix, while it also houses mechanoreceptors for touch, thermoreceptors for heat, and various glands such as hair follicles, sweat glands, sebaceous glands, and apocrine glands. Furthermore, the dermis contains blood vessels that supply nourishment and facilitate waste removal for both dermal and epidermal cells.
title: Dermis

text: Securities and Exchange Board of India's chairman is Ajay Tyagi, who was appointed on 10 January 2017 to replace U K Sinha and officially took charge on 1 March 2017. The Board comprises Ajay Tyagi.
title: Securities and Exchange Board of India

text: Real Madrid had the most success in the European Cup, winning the trophy for a record twelve times. The club has also won the UEFA Cup twice, in 1985 and 1986, the Super Cup four times, in 2002, 2014, 2016 and 2017, the Intercontinental Cup three times, in 1960, 1998 and 2002, and the FIFA Club World Cup three times, in 2014, 2016 and 2017. Real Madrid, with 24 trophies, is the most successful European team in international football. They have also been involved in European football ever since they became the first Spanish club to enter the European Cup in 1955, except for the 1977–78 and 1996–97 seasons.
title: Real Madrid C.F. in international football competitions

title: Kudzu in the United States

title: Darlene Cates

title: Vikings (season 4)

text: The Premier League Golden Boot is awarded to the player who scores the most goals in a season, though in rare cases where two or more players tie for the top count, the award is shared among them. For instance, in the 1993–94 and 1994–95 seasons, Andy Cole and Shearer both scored 34 goals, resulting in a shared award. Similarly, during the 1997–98 and 1998–99 seasons, the lowest number of goals ever recorded for the award was 18, achieved when the prize was split between three players. The last time the award was shared was in the 2010–11 season, where Dimitar Berbatov and Carlos Tevez both scored 20 goals. Additionally, Harry Kane holds the record for the highest goals-to-games ratio, scoring 29 goals in 30 games during the 2016–17 season.
title: Premier League Golden Boot

text: Frank Theodore "Ted" Levine, an American actor born in 1957, is best known for his role as Buffalo Bill in the film *The Silence of the Lambs* and for playing Captain Leland Stottlemeyer in the television series *Monk*.
title: Ted Levine

Fox and Christopher Lloyd.

The movie follows five teenagers from various high school cliques who spend a Saturday in detention together, ultimately breaking away from their stereotypes while confronting a strict disciplinarian.

text: The film *The Breakfast Club* premiered in Los Angeles on February 7, 1985, and was subsequently released in cinemas by Universal Pictures on February 15, 1985. Critics consider this movie one of the greatest high school films of all time, as well as one of Hughes' most memorable and recognizable works.

text: A typical adult possesses a blood volume of approximately 5 liters, a figure that is generally lower in females compared to males. This volume is primarily regulated by the kidneys, which play a crucial role in maintaining the body's fluid balance.
title: Blood volume

text: By late 1922, the German defaults on payments had grown so regular that a crisis engulfed the Reparations Commission; the French and Belgian delegates urged occupying the Ruhr as a way of forcing Germany to pay more, while the British delegate urged a lowering of the payments. As a consequence of a German default on timber deliveries in December 1922, the Reparations Commission declared Germany in default, which led to the Franco-Belgian occupation of the Ruhr in January 1923. Particularly galling to the French was that the timber quota the Germans defaulted on was based on an assessment of their capacity the Germans made themselves and subsequently lowered. The entire conflict was further exacerbated by a German default on coal deliveries in early January 1923, which was the thirty-fourth coal default in the previous thirty-six months. The French Premier Raymond Poincaré was deeply reluctant to order the Ruhr occupation and took this step only after the British had rejected his proposals for non-military sanctions against Germany. Frustrated at Germany not paying reparations, Poincaré hoped for joint Anglo-French economic sanctions against Germany in 1922 and opposed military action. However, by December 1922 he was faced with Anglo-American-German opposition and saw coal for French steel production and payments in money as laid out in the Treaty of Versailles draining away. Poincaré was exasperated with British opposition, and wrote to the French ambassador in London:
title: Occupation of the Ruhr

text: The occupation of the Ruhr was initiated by French Prime Minister Raymond Poincaré and took place on 11 January 1923. General Alphonse Caron's 32nd infantry corps, under the supervision of General Jean-Marie Degoutte, carried out the operation. Some theories suggest the French aimed to occupy the centre of German coal, iron, and steel production in the Ruhr area valley simply to get the money, while others state that France did it to ensure that the reparations were paid in goods because the Mark was practically worthless due to hyperinflation that already existed at the end of 1922. France had the iron ore and Germany had the coal, and each state wanted free access to the resource it was short of, as together these resources had far more value than separately. (Eventually this problem was resolved in the post-World War II European Coal and Steel community.)
title: Occupation of the Ruhr

text: Once More, with Feeling (Buffy the Vampire Slayer) features a scene where Buffy tells her friends she was in heaven. When asked by Sweet what she thinks about life, Buffy gives her pessimistic take on its meaning ("Something to Sing About"). When the others arrive, she divulges that Willow took her from heaven, and Willow reacts with horror at finding out what she's done. Upon divulging this truth, Buffy gives up on singing and dances so frenetically that she begins to smoke — on the verge of combusting as Sweet's other victims have been shown to do — until Spike stops her, telling her that the only way to go forward is to just keep living her life. Xander then reveals that he, not Dawn, called Sweet, hoping he would be shown a happy ending for his marriage plans. Sweet, after releasing Xander from the obligation to be Sweet's "bride", tells the group how much fun they have been ("What You Feel—Reprise") and disappears. The Scoobies realize that their relationships have been changed irreversibly by the secrets revealed in their songs ("Where Do We Go from Here?"). Spike leaves The Bronze, but Buffy follows him out, and they kiss ("Coda").
title: Once More, with Feeling (Buffy the Vampire Slayer)

text: The recipient of the inaugural Jnanpith Award was the Malayalam author G. Sankara Kurup, who received the prize in 1965 for his collection of poems, Odakkuzhal (The Bamboo Flute), originally published in 1950.
title: Jnanpith Award

text: The term "synapse" was introduced in 1897 by the English neurophysiologist Charles Sherrington, who struggled to find a word that emphasized a union between two separate elements. This concept was described in Michael Foster's Textbook of Physiology, where Sherrington proposed that neurons communicate with each other through chemicals, a discovery that established the fundamental mechanism of neural communication.
title: Synapse

text: Gestalt psychology, also known as gestaltism, is a philosophy of mind belonging to the Berlin School of experimental psychology. This school of thought attempts to understand the laws governing the acquisition and maintenance of meaningful perceptions within an apparently chaotic world. A central tenet of this theory is that the mind forms a global whole with inherent self-organizing tendencies. While the physiological mechanisms underlying Gestalt theory are poorly defined and lack supporting evidence, the school has faced criticism for being descriptive of perceptual end products without offering sufficient insight into the underlying processes.
title: Gestalt psychology

text: Long John Silver, a cunning and opportunistic pirate who served as quartermaster under the notorious Captain Flint, claimed to have served in the Royal Navy. He lost his leg during an incident involving the "immortal Hawke," where his left leg was cut off close by the hip and under the left shoulder. Despite this disability, Silver managed to carry a crutch with wonderful dexterity, hopping about upon it like a bird. He was very tall and strong, with a face as big as a ham, yet he remained intelligent and smiling.
title: Long John Silver

text: In the 2011 NBA Finals, the Western Conference champion Dallas Mavericks defeated the Eastern Conference champion Miami Heat 4 to 2, securing their first NBA championship title. This victory marked a significant milestone for the Mavericks as the last NBA team from Texas to win its first title, following the Houston Rockets' back-to-back championships in 1994 and 1995. The series also highlighted the Lakers' absence, as it was the first time in four years they did not make the Finals after being swept in the Western Conference semifinals by the eventual champion Dallas Mavericks.
title: 2011 NBA Finals

text: Sneaky Pete is an American crime drama series created by David Shore and Bryan Cranston, which follows Marius Josipović, an ex-convict who adopts the identity of his cellmate Pete Murphy to escape his past. The show stars Giovanni Ribisi as the main character, alongside other cast members like Marin Ireland, Shane McRae, and Libe Barer. Originally set to debut on August 7, 2015, the pilot was followed by a full series order that September. Shore departed from the project in early 2016, leaving the role of showrunner to Graham Yost, who continued as executive producer for the remaining nine episodes. The first season premiered on January 13, 2017, exclusively on Amazon Video, and the series was renewed for a second season on January 19, 2017, which aired on March 9, 2018.
title: Sneaky Pete

text: A 1994 film titled My Summer Story, which serves as the sequel to the classic holiday movie It Runs in the Family, recounts the ongoing adventures of the Parker family. This narrative is an adaptation of semi-autobiographical tales by Jean Shepherd, primarily drawn from his book In God We Trust, All Others Pay Cash.
title: My Summer Story

text: Virgin Australia Airlines Pty Ltd, formerly known as Virgin Blue Airlines, is Australia's second-largest carrier after Qantas[3] and holds the distinction of being the largest operator by fleet size to utilize the 'Virgin' brand. Situated in Bowen Hills, Brisbane, the company was co-founded by British entrepreneur Richard Branson, who also founded the parent Virgin Group and previously served as CEO of Virgin Blue. The entity was officially established in November 1999[4] with only two aircraft operating on a single route, before rapidly gaining prominence as Australia's second-largest airline following the collapse of Ansett Australia in September 2001. Over time, the airline has expanded to directly serve 29 cities across Australia, utilizing a fleet of narrow-body Boeing and Embraer jets, as well as widebody aircraft from Airbus and Boeing.
title: Virgin Australia

text: The first book of the Percy Jackson series is titled The Lightning Thief, which was written by Rick Riordan over the course of a year after his son, Haley, requested bedtime stories based on Greek mythology.

Written by Gibson herself in 1984, two years before the recording, the dance-pop track reached number four on the U.S. Billboard Hot 100 chart in the summer of 1987.
title: Only in My Dreams

text: Alabama is nicknamed the Yellowhammer State, after the state bird, and is also known as the "Heart of Dixie" and the Cotton State. The state tree is the longleaf pine, and the state flower is the camellia. While the largest city by population is Birmingham, the state capital is Montgomery. The largest city by land area is Huntsville, and the oldest city is Mobile, which was founded by French colonists in 1702.
title: Alabama

text: While the native origin of coffee is thought to be Ethiopia, the earliest substantiated evidence regarding either its drinking or the coffee tree itself dates to the 15th century. This period marks the beginning of the coffee's journey from Yemen, where it was first cultivated by Sufi monks, before eventually spreading across the Middle East, South India, Persia, Turkey, and northern Africa in the following century.
title: History of coffee

text: The earliest credible evidence of either coffee drinking or knowledge of the coffee tree appears in the middle of the 15th century, in Yemen's Sufi monasteries, where this beverage was first introduced to the wider world.
title: History of coffee

text: Tim Hortons initially opened its first United States locations in Deerfield Beach and Pompano Beach, Florida, in 1981. Although these initial stores proved unsuccessful and were subsequently closed, the brand returned to the US in 1985 with a location in Amherst, New York. Starting in the mid-1990s, the chain expanded further by acquiring former locations from fast food chains such as Rax Restaurants, Hardee's, and Bess Eaton, eventually establishing numerous stores across various markets including Maine and Buffalo.
title: Tim Hortons

text: The Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire stands as one of the most significant campaigns in the Spanish colonization of the Americas. Following years of preliminary exploration and military engagements, 180 Spanish soldiers led by conquistador Francisco Pizarro, along with his brothers and native allies, captured the Sapa Inca Atahualpa during the 1532 Battle of Cajamarca. This pivotal event marked the beginning of a long campaign that spanned decades of fighting, ultimately culminating in Spanish victory in 1572 and the establishment of the Viceroyalty of Peru. Consequently, the conquest of the Inca Empire, known as "Tahuantinsuyu" or "Tawantinsuyu" in Quechua for "Realm of the Four Parts," spurred subsequent expeditions into present-day Chile and Colombia and even ventured toward the Amazon Basin.
title: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire

text: Jason Paige, an American singer born on January 6, 1969, is best known for his role as the primary vocalist for the opening theme of the first season of the Pokémon TV series.
title: Jason Paige

text: Named as the Northern Pacific Ocean, wild caught sockeye salmon are anadromous species of salmon found in the Northern Pacific Ocean and rivers discharging into it. This Pacific salmon species is primarily red in hue during spawning and can grow up to 84 cm (2 ft 9 in) in length and weigh 2.3 to 7 kg (5.1–15.4 lb). Juveniles remain in freshwater until they are ready to migrate to the ocean, over distances of up to 1,600 km (990 mi). Their diet consists primarily of zooplankton. Sockeye salmon are semelparous, dying after they spawn. Some populations, referred to as kokanee, do not migrate to the ocean and live their entire lives in freshwater.
title: Sockeye salmon

text: In 1969, to accommodate an expanding number of reporters assigned to the White House, President Richard Nixon utilized the indoor swimming pool that had been installed by the March of Dimes for Franklin D. Roosevelt. This facility was subsequently covered and repurposed to serve as press offices and a lounge capable of functioning as a briefing room.
title: James S. Brady Press Briefing Room

text: The Zoroastrian religion, also known as the Zoroastrian faith, was the dominant religious tradition in Persia prior to the arrival of Islam.
title: Muslim conquest of Persia

text: Kerosene oil rises within the wick of a lantern through a process known as capillary action. This mechanism draws the fuel upward, enabling the lamp to function effectively.
title: Kerosene lamp

text: Proinsulin undergoes post translational modification to become mature insulin, a process that occurs exclusively within the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans. When proinsulin is transported through the Golgi apparatus, the C-peptide is cleaved by two endoproteases: PC1 and PC3, which disrupt the C peptide-B chain connection, and PC2, a type II endoprotease, which cleaves the C peptide-A chain bond. The resulting molecule, now mature insulin, is stored as a hexamer in secretory vesicles and stabilized with $Zn^{2+}$ molecules until it is secreted.
title: Proinsulin

text: Fructose, or fruit sugar, is a simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants. While it is often bonded to glucose to form sucrose, it is one of three dietary monosaccharides absorbed directly into the blood during digestion, alongside glucose and galactose. First discovered by French chemist Augustin-Pierre Dubrunfaut in 1847 and named by English chemist William Allen Miller in 1857, pure fructose is a sweet, white, odorless, crystalline solid. It stands out as the most water-soluble of all sugars, with notable presence in honey, tree and vine fruits, flowers, berries, and most root vegetables.
title: Fructose

text: In the film Little Shop of Horrors, Seymour Krelborn and his colleague Audrey work at Mushnik's Flower Shop in a run-down neighborhood known as Skid Row. When struggling from a lack of customers, Seymour decides to close the store, but Audrey suggests he may have more success by displaying an unusual plant he owns. Immediately attracting a customer, Seymour explains he bought the plant, which he dubbed "Audrey II," from a Chinese flower shop during a solar eclipse. This plant soon starts dying, worrying Seymour, and accidentally pricking his finger, he discovers that Audrey II needs human blood to thrive.
title: Little Shop of Horrors (film)

title: Confederation Bridge

title: United Kingdom–United States relations

text: The Man with the Golden Gun (soundtrack) features a theme tune performed by Lulu, composed by John Barry, and the lyrics to the song were written by Don Black. text: The type I error rate, or significance level, represents the probability of rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true. This probability is denoted by the Greek letter alpha (alpha) and is commonly set to 0.05 (5%), which implies that it is acceptable to have a 5% chance of incorrectly rejecting the null hypothesis.
title: Type I and type II errors

text: Lōʻihi Seamount (also known as Lōʻihi) is an active submarine volcano located approximately 35 kilometers (22 miles) off the southeast coast of the island of Hawaii. The top of this seamount sits about 975 meters (3,000 feet) below sea level. This volcanic structure sits on the flank of Mauna Loa, the largest shield volcano on Earth. The name Lōihi, meaning "long" in Hawaiian, refers to the fact that it is the newest volcano in the Hawaiian-Emperor seamount chain, a string of volcanoes stretching over 5,800 kilometers (3,600 miles) northwest of Lōʻihi. Unlike most active volcanoes in the Pacific Ocean that form on the Pacific Ring of Fire, Lōʻihi and the other volcanoes of the Hawaiian-Emperor chain are hotspot volcanoes formed well away from the nearest plate boundary. Volcanoes in the Hawaiian Islands arise from the Hawaii hotspot, and as the youngest volcano in the chain, Lōihi is the only Hawaiian volcano currently in the deep submarine preshield stage of development.
title: Lōʻihi Seamount

text: The Second Temple was reconstructed under Herod, who initiated a massive expansion of the Temple Mount. Although religious worship and rituals persisted throughout this construction process, the project was halted when the Roman emperor Caligula intended to install his own statue inside the temple. In response, Herod's grandson Agrippa I successfully intervened and persuaded Caligula to abandon the plan.
title: Second Temple

text: Nathan Hale, a soldier who served as a spy for the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War, was captured by the British forces and subsequently executed. While not a hero in the traditional sense, he is remembered today as an American hero, a status officially conferred upon him in 1985.
title: Nathan Hale

text: "Cliff Richard" is the artist who performed the song "Suddenly" alongside Olivia Newton-John on the soundtrack album Xanadu, which serves as the love theme for the 1980 film of the same name. The track was written by John Farrar and produced by him, and it was released on Jet Records, reaching No. 15 in the UK charts in October 1980 and No. 20 in the US. The accompanying video captures the duo singing the song to each other in a penthouse setting.
title: Suddenly (Olivia Newton-John and Cliff Richard song)

text: Command Sergeant Major Daniel A. Dailey served as the head of the Army's senior enlisted and administrative staff, succeeding Raymond F. Chandler III on January 30, 2015. He held the rank of Sergeant Major of the Army from January 15, 2004, through February 28, 2011, and remained in that position for the longest tenure among all incumbents, serving longer than four years.
title: Sergeant Major of the Army

text: In the original 1968 film *The Thomas Crown Affair*, the song "The Windmills of Your Mind" is credited to singer Noel Harrison, who performed it during the opening credits. During the film's plot, the character Thomas Crown flies a glider at the glider airport in Salem, New Hampshire; Norman Jewison, the film's producer and director, commissioned an original song for this scene to reflect the protagonist's ambivalent feelings while he prepares to commit a major robbery. Although Alan Bergman recalled that Michel Legrand played seven or eight melodies for the Bergmans, they selected the same baroque melody for the song, which was written with a stream-of-consciousness lyric intended to create a "mind trip." The song's title originated from a line at the end of a section that the writers felt needed to be repeated, and the final version restructured the lyrics so that the title appeared again at the conclusion of the piece.
title: The Windmills of Your Mind

text: "Los Lonely Boys" is the title of the debut single released by the American rock band, which features the song "Heaven." The track was composed by brothers Henry, Jojo, and Ringo Garza, the core members of the group, and it was included on their multi-platinum self-titled album.
title: Heaven (Los Lonely Boys song)

text: The Organ Mountains are a rugged mountain range located in southern New Mexico within the Southwestern United States. These mountains lie approximately 10 miles (16 km) east of the city of Las Cruces in Doña Ana County. Organ Mountains-Desert Peaks National Monument was officially declared a national monument on May 21, 2014.
title: Organ Mountains (New Mexico)

text: Kate Warne, the pioneering figure of the Pinkerton Detective Agency, served as the agency's inaugural female detective in 1856, marking a historic milestone for the United States.
title: Kate Warne

text: The World Economic Forum is best known for its annual meeting, which takes place at the end of January in Davos, a mountain resort located in Graubünden within the eastern Alps region of Switzerland. This gathering brings together approximately 2,500 top business leaders, international political leaders, economists, celebrities, and journalists for up to four days to discuss the most pressing issues facing the world. Often this specific location alone is used to identify meetings, participation, and participants, with phrases such as "a Davos panel" and "Davos man" frequently used to refer to attendees.
title: World Economic Forum

text: In 2018, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi gave the plenary speech becoming the first head of state from India to deliver the inaugural keynote for the annual meet at Davos.
title: World Economic Forum

text: Gareth Barry has made the most Premier League appearances, surpassing the previous record holder Ryan Giggs. Barry achieved this milestone by playing his 633rd match for West Bromwich Albion against Arsenal on 25 September 2017. At the time of this record-breaking performance, Barry ranked eighth in English top division appearances since the Second World War, trailing Giggs in sixth place with a total of 672 top division appearances.
title: List of Premier League players with 500 or more appearances

text: Since 1947, the state's political leadership has been governed by eight Chief Ministers, with the inaugural leader being Prafulla Chandra Ghosh. This Indian National Congress leader was succeeded by his party-mates Dr Bidhan Chandra Roy and Prafulla Chandra Sen. A decade of instability followed, characterized by fractious coalition governments and frequent impositions of President's rule, before the situation stabilized with the 1977 election victory of the Communist Party of India (Marxist). Under the leadership of Jyoti Basu, the CPM-led Left Front government ruled for over 23 years (1977–2000). Subsequent rule in West Bengal continued for another 10 years under Buddhadeb Bhattacharya, who was defeated in the 2011 election by the Trinamool Congress. Appointed on 20 May 2011, Trinamool leader Mamata Banerjee is the current incumbent, the state's first woman chief minister.
title: List of Chief Ministers of West Bengal

text: The Hunger Games is a 2008 dystopian novel written by the American author Suzanne Collins. This work tells the story of 16-year-old Katniss Everdeen, who inhabits the future, post-apocalyptic nation of Panem located in North America. In this society, the Capitol exerts political control over the twelve districts surrounding it. The narrative follows an annual event where one boy and one girl, aged 12 to 18, are selected by lottery to compete in a televised battle to the death.
title: The Hunger Games (novel)

title: The Hunger Games (novel)

title: IEEE 802.11

text: Muhammad is recognized as the founder of Islam, as he began receiving divine revelations in 610 CE and established the message that eventually attracted followers despite opposition from Meccan notables. Following the death of his influential uncle Abu Talib in 618, Muhammad migrated to Yathrib (Medina) and later died in 632, an event that triggered a succession dispute over who would lead the Muslim community, a conflict that intensified after the Battle of Karbala and the subsequent killing of his grandson Hussein ibn Ali.
title: History of Islam

text: According to tradition, the Islamic prophet Muhammad was born in Mecca around the year 570. He was a member of the Quraysh family, and when he was approximately forty years old, he began receiving divine revelations through the angel Gabriel. These messages, which eventually formed the Quran, instructed him to establish a strict monotheistic faith, warn his neighbors about the Day of Judgment, and address social injustices within his city. Although his initial message attracted only a small group of followers and faced increasing opposition from influential notables in Mecca, Muhammad eventually fled to Yathrib (later known as Medina) after losing protection following the death of his uncle Abu Talib, where he was welcomed by his community. This pivotal migration, historically termed the hijra, marks the beginning of the Islamic era.
title: History of Islam

text: Sasuke Uchiha was seven years old when his clan died.
title: Sasuke Uchiha

Davis, pastor of New Birth Birmingham in Birmingham, Alabama, would be Long's successor at New Birth Missionary Baptist Church in Lithonia while remaining pastor of the Birmingham church.

Although the ELT was once a Soviet-backed Marxist guerrilla group, it lost its financial support following the dissolution of the USSR in 1991, leading the group to turn to kidnapping for ransom. While the movie's map depicts Ecuador, the actual location chosen for the capital city Quito is situated in the Ecuadorian Andes, alongside the eastern jungle and the nearby city of Baños de Agua Santa.

text: Cadbury, previously known as Cadbury's, is a British multinational confectionery firm that has been owned by Mondelez International since 2010. As the second-largest confectionery brand globally following Wrigley's, the company operates in more than 50 countries worldwide. Notably, in 2013, The Daily Telegraph listed Cadbury among Britain's most successful exports, having produced iconic items such as Dairy Milk chocolate and the Creme Egg selection box.

text: On 23 November 1996, Ethiopian Airlines Flight 961, a Boeing 767-200ER, was hijacked by three individuals seeking asylum in Australia while en route from Addis Ababa to Nairobi. The aircraft subsequently crashed into the Indian Ocean near Grande Comore, Comoros Islands, resulting in the loss of 125 of the 175 people on board, including the hijackers. An official investigation concluded that four of the surviving passengers remained uninjured, though the remainder sustained injuries.
title: Ethiopian Airlines Flight 961

text: My Country My Life is an autobiographical book written by L. K. Advani, an Indian politician who served as the Deputy Prime Minister of India from 2002 to 2004 and was the Leader of the Opposition in the 15th Lok Sabha. The book was released on 19 March 2008 by Abdul Kalam, the eleventh President of India, and contains 1,040 pages that narrate autobiographical accounts and events in the life of Advani. It became the best-selling non-fiction book, with Advani joining Archer as a bestseller author, and the book website claims it sold an excess of 1,000,000 copies. The publication also covers events in Indian politics and history from 1900 to the present day.

text: The Dominican Independence War secured the Republic of Spanish Haiti's autonomy from Haiti on February 27, 1844. Prior to this conflict, the island of Hispaniola had been united under the Haitian government for twenty-two years following its invasion of the newly independent nation in 1822. Before the war, the island was known as the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo, where the criollo class overthrew the Spanish crown in 1821 and subsequently unified with Haiti.
title: Dominican War of Independence

text: "Jeanie with the Light Brown Hair" is a parlor song written by Stephen Foster, who lived from 1826 to 1864. The piece was published by Firth, Pond & Co. in New York in 1854. The composer created the lyrics while thinking of his estranged wife, Jane McDowell, who is the subject of the famous title.
title: Jeanie with the Light Brown Hair

text: The Bob & Tom Show is a syndicated US radio program established by Bob Kevoian and Tom Griswold at radio station WFBQ in Indianapolis, Indiana on March 7, 1983, and has been syndicated nationally since January 6, 1995. Originally aired by Premiere Networks, the program moved to Cumulus Media Networks (now Westwood One) at the beginning of 2014.

text: The frontal lobe is the part of the brain responsible for complex thinking, as it handles the ability to project future consequences from current actions, makes choices between good and bad actions, and suppresses socially unacceptable responses.
title: Frontal lobe

text: The 2016 UEFA Champions League Final was the final match of the 2015–16 season, the 61st year of Europe's premier club football tournament organized by UEFA. This event took place at the San Siro stadium in Milan, Italy, on May 28, 2016, between Spanish teams Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid. Real Madrid won the match 5–3 on a penalty shoot-out after a 1–1 draw in extra time, securing a record-extending 11th title in the competition.

The music was composed by lead vocalist and guitarist Patrick Stump, with all lyrics penned by bassist Pete Wentz, continuing the band's songwriting approach they took for some songs on their prior 2003 effort Take This to Your Grave. Neal Avron handled production duties. Commenting on the record's lyrical themes, Wentz said the lyrics were about "the anxiety and depression that goes along with looking at your own life."

text: The separation of the Korean peninsula into North and South occurred in 1945, the year following World War II when the Empire of Japan's 35-year rule ended. Consequently, the United States and the Soviet Union each occupied one of the two regions, establishing a boundary along the 38th parallel.
title: Division of Korea

text: On August 8, 1945, the Soviet Union declared war on Japan, a move that occurred two days after the atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima and three months to the day after the end of hostilities in Europe. In response to the rapid advance of Soviet troops, the US government assigned two young officers, Dean Rusk and Charles Bonesteel, to define an American occupation zone. Working on extremely short notice and completely unprepared, they used a National Geographic map to decide on the 38th parallel. They chose this line because it divided the country approximately in half but would place the capital Seoul under American control. No experts on Korea were consulted, and the two men were unaware that forty years before, Japan and pre-revolutionary Russia had discussed sharing Korea along the same parallel. The division placed sixteen million Koreans in the American zone and nine million in the Soviet zone. To the surprise of the Americans, the Soviet Union immediately accepted the division. The agreement was incorporated into General Order No. 1, which was approved on 17 August 1945 for the surrender of Japan.
title: Division of Korea

text: According to the Origination Clause of the United States Constitution, all bills for raising revenue, generally tax bills, must originate in the House of Representatives, similar to the Westminster system requirement that all money bills originate in the lower house. Traditionally, though, appropriation bills also originate in the House of Representatives. The title of the original source document is Appropriation bill. In reference to revenue bills, the Constitution also states that the "Senate may propose or concur with Amendments as on other Bills." As with revenue bills, the Senate and House each drafts and considers its own appropriation bill. The Senate then "cuts-and-pastes," substituting the language of its version of a particular appropriation bill for the language of the House bill, then agrees to the bill as amended.
title: Appropriation bill

text: As of 2015–16, the iPhone 5S retained a 4-inch screen size, which had been a key selling point for a significant number of customers. Apple highlighted that 30 million 4-inch iPhones were sold in 2015, marking the form factor's peak popularity before it was overtaken by the larger display 4.7/5.5-inch iPhone 6 and 6 Plus released in September 2014. While the 5S was viewed as a premium benchmark with its gold finish, the subsequent 6 and 6S designs faced criticism for feeling like a "slick $650 bar of soap." Although the iPhone 5 was praised for its elegant aluminum and glass combination, the 5S's design proved less scalable than the 6/6S models, which better accommodated the growing consumer trend toward larger screen sizes. Consequently, when Apple discontinued the iPhone 5S, it was replaced by the iPhone SE, which outwardly resembles the 5S despite having significantly upgraded internal hardware.
title: iPhone 5S

text: Apoptosis is a highly regulated process that cannot be halted once it has begun. This cell death mechanism can be initiated through one of two pathways: the intrinsic pathway, where a cell kills itself due to internal stress, or the extrinsic pathway, where the cell kills itself because of signals from other cells. Both pathways ultimately activate caspases, which are proteases or enzymes that degrade proteins. The process begins when both pathways activate initiator caspases, which subsequently activate executioner caspases. These executioner caspases then kill the cell by degrading proteins indiscriminately.
title: Apoptosis

text: According to Indian folklore, the city of Delhi served as the magnificent and opulent capital of the Pandavas in the Indian epic Mahabharata, a status established around 3500 BC. While a 16th-century Persian historian, Firishta, recorded a tradition that Delhi or Dilli was founded by a Raja Dhilu prior to the Greek invasions, it is important to note that contemporary kings referred to the initial Muslim invaders as Yavanas. Despite this historical nuance, the primary answer remains that the Pandavas are the figures credited with making Delhi the capital.
title: History of Delhi

text: Jack Ryan was born in Baltimore, Maryland, in 1950, the son of Emmet William Ryan, a Baltimore City Police Department homicide lieutenant, and World War II veteran.
title: Jack Ryan (character)

text: T.S. Eliot is the primary figure associated with the theory of the objective correlative in literature. His essay "Hamlet and His Problems," republished in *The Sacred Wood: Essays on Poetry and Criticism*, details his view on Shakespeare's incomplete development of Hamlet's emotions, serving as a foundational example of the concept. In this work, Eliot defines the artistic "inevitability" as the complete adequacy of external factors to an emotion, contrasting this with Hamlet's lack of sufficient supporting story and characters. While Plato first distinguished between mimesis and diegesis, Eliot's theory suggests the objective correlative is merely an ancient distinction between these two forms. According to Formalist critics, this method of creating emotion through external evidence should produce the author's detachment from the depicted character, uniting the literary work's emotion. The "occasion" of E. Montale is identified as another form of correlative.
title: Objective correlative

text: In the biological classification system developed by Carl Woese, the tree of life is structured around three primary domains. While the first two groups, Archaea and Bacteria, consist of prokaryotic organisms lacking a nucleus, the third domain encompasses all multicellular life possessing a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Consequently, humans belong to the domain Eukarya.
title: Domain (biology)

The key participants in this historical event were the nationalists of the Union, who pledged allegiance to the U.S. Constitution, against the secessionists of the Confederate States who fought for the expansion of slavery.
